heading: Semantic design rules
text: - **UNB-KNOW-001:** All canonical entities, claims, relations and decisions have stable opaque IDs and explicit namespaces.

heading: Semantic design rules
text: - **UNB-KNOW-002:** Support bitemporal semantics: when a fact was true/effective versus when Unbound learned/recorded it.

heading: Semantic design rules
text: - **UNB-KNOW-003:** Preserve conflicting claims and differing source authority; do not collapse into one unqualified truth field.

heading: Semantic design rules
text: - **UNB-KNOW-004:** Explicitly distinguish unknown, absent from source, not applicable, stale, disputed, and verified false.

heading: Semantic design rules
text: - **UNB-KNOW-005:** Confidence applies to a specific claim/matching inference, not a universal charity trust score; separate statistical score from deterministic legal eligibility.

heading: Semantic design rules
text: - **UNB-KNOW-006:** Maintain typed ontology/controlled predicates with versioned definitions, provenance and unit validation, including financial periods and fiscal-year basis.

heading: Semantic design rules
text: - **UNB-KNOW-007:** Support legal entity vs program/project vs fiscal sponsor vs local chapter as separate nodes and roles.

heading: Semantic design rules
text: - **UNB-KNOW-008:** Reversible identity merges/splits preserve original records, external IDs, prior grants, references and history.

heading: Semantic design rules
text: - **UNB-KNOW-009:** Model financial observations with reporting period, filing version/amendment, currency, measurement definition and source, not only amount.

heading: Semantic design rules
text: - **UNB-KNOW-010:** Model privacy, licensing, redistribution, AI-use and retention permissions as enforceable attributes inherited from evidence into derived outputs.

heading: Semantic design rules
text: - **UNB-KNOW-011:** Preserve source language and normalized translations separately, with translation provenance.

heading: Semantic design rules
text: - **UNB-KNOW-012:** Cross-partner canonical public facts may be shared only when lawful; sponsor-private claims, reviews, bank details and grant relationships remain isolated.

heading: Semantic design rules
text: - **UNB-KNOW-013:** An organization may dispute an internal claim; adjudication produces linked correction, not deletion of immutable required history.

heading: Semantic design rules
text: - **UNB-KNOW-014:** All authoritative history is append-only, using Strata where verified and approved; projections/search indexes can be rebuilt.

heading: Semantic design rules
text: - **UNB-KNOW-015:** Every externally surfaced claim supports a traceable evidence chain, freshness status, rights status and correction path.

heading: Semantic design rules
text: - **UNB-KNOW-016:** Define a knowledge compiler/export contract for deterministic typed F# models and agent-readable projections, evaluating integration with echelon-knowledge-store rather than assuming its implementation or capabilities.

heading: Identity resolution
text: - **UNB-KNOW-017:** Exact identifier match is a strong candidate signal, not unconditional auto-merge; consider issuer, jurisdiction, validity and conflicting legal entities.

heading: Identity resolution
text: - **UNB-KNOW-018:** Use normalized names, aliases, addresses, websites, officers and historical relationships as reviewable probabilistic evidence; never merge solely on similarity.

heading: Identity resolution
text: - **UNB-KNOW-019:** Maintain gold-standard matching evaluation sets with false merge, missed match, precision/recall, ambiguity and high-risk collision measures.

heading: Identity resolution
text: - **UNB-KNOW-020:** High-risk merges and splits require steward review, dual control where material, and reversible lineage.

heading: Identity resolution
text: - **UNB-KNOW-021:** Fiscal sponsor/project identity and legal payee identity must remain distinguishable for grant eligibility and future payment execution.

heading: Identity resolution
text: - **UNB-KNOW-022:** Cross-jurisdiction entity matching must retain original language, transliteration, country, issuer and registration validity.

heading: Source orchestration and economics
text: - **UNB-KNOW-023:** Prefer official bulk downloads and APIs, then lawful structured feeds, then permitted web extraction, then direct charity submission; avoid bypassing technical or contractual controls.

heading: Source orchestration and economics
text: - **UNB-KNOW-024:** Each connector declares retrieval limits, rights, costs, authentication, retry, backoff, source update cadence, schema version and failure handling.

heading: Source orchestration and economics
text: - **UNB-KNOW-025:** Schedule acquisition by volatility and decision criticality, not one global refresh cadence; support event-driven recheck for high-risk grant decisions.

heading: Source orchestration and economics
text: - **UNB-KNOW-026:** Source drift, parser regression, empty feeds, implausible record deltas and stale records trigger quarantine/alerts.

heading: Source orchestration and economics
text: - **UNB-KNOW-027:** Every ingestion is resumable and idempotent; duplicate/out-of-order observations do not overwrite prior evidence.

heading: Source orchestration and economics
text: - **UNB-KNOW-028:** Maintain source coverage matrix across US federal, 50 states, DC, territories and selected foreign jurisdictions with verified access and gaps.

heading: Source orchestration and economics
text: - **UNB-KNOW-029:** Track acquisition/compute/storage/review cost per source and downstream decision utility, without discarding strategically valuable long-tail data solely for short-term ROI.

heading: Source orchestration and economics
text: - **UNB-KNOW-030:** Distinguish machine extraction from human attestation and independent verification; AI may extract candidate claims but not fabricate provenance.

heading: Source orchestration and economics
text: - **UNB-KNOW-031:** Provide freshness and confidence propagation into downstream APIs and decision policies.

heading: Source orchestration and economics
text: - **UNB-KNOW-032:** Use deterministic reconciliation to detect contradictory government records, amendments and retroactive status changes.

heading: Interfaces and operations
text: - **UNB-KNOW-033:** Versioned APIs for source registry, acquisition jobs, evidence lookup, claims, canonical identities, relationship graph, verification cases, snapshots and eligibility evaluation.

heading: Interfaces and operations
text: - **UNB-KNOW-034:** Forma provides accessible mobile-first stewardship workspace with source comparisons, merge/split previews, conflicts, queues, evidence and rights/freshness badges.

heading: Interfaces and operations
text: - **UNB-KNOW-035:** Folio produces reproducible charity dossier, source coverage, identity decision, eligibility audit and contradiction reports.

heading: Interfaces and operations
text: - **UNB-KNOW-036:** All tools enforce field-level privacy, source-rights controls, tenant/partner authorization, least privilege, immutable audit and explicit external disclosure policy.

heading: Interfaces and operations
text: - **UNB-KNOW-037:** The graph/search/semantic index is a derived projection, not the authoritative source of truth.

heading: Interfaces and operations
text: - **UNB-KNOW-038:** Preserve interoperability through versioned schema exports and authorized data portability without redistributing restricted source content.

heading: Interfaces and operations
text: - **UNB-KNOW-039:** Source and knowledge health dashboards measure coverage, freshness, unresolved conflicts, review queues, false merges, data quality and decision impact.

heading: Interfaces and operations
text: - **UNB-KNOW-040:** Do not enable a public/commercial intelligence API until licensing, privacy, reliability, security and governance gates are independently approved.

heading: Critical acceptance scenarios
text: KNOW-T01: Conflicting IRS and state records remain visible with valid and recorded timestamps; sponsor decision identifies applicable authority.

heading: Critical acceptance scenarios
text: KNOW-T02: Two same-name charities with distinct IDs do not merge.

heading: Critical acceptance scenarios
text: KNOW-T03: A charity project under a fiscal sponsor has separate project, legal payee and eligible entity records.

heading: Critical acceptance scenarios
text: KNOW-T04: An amended filing changes historical figures; both filings and downstream analyses remain reproducible.

heading: Critical acceptance scenarios
text: KNOW-T05: A later-received revocation with retroactive effective date triggers time-aware reevaluation, not silent historical rewrite.

heading: Critical acceptance scenarios
text: KNOW-T06: A source's rights prohibit redistribution; exports and AI responses enforce it.

heading: Critical acceptance scenarios
text: KNOW-T07: An AI extraction invents an officer name; unsupported claim is rejected/quarantined.

heading: Critical acceptance scenarios
text: KNOW-T08: A bad identity merge is reversed while preserving grants and historical references.

heading: Critical acceptance scenarios
text: KNOW-T09: Source outage leaves known-last data marked stale; freshness-sensitive approvals are held.

heading: Critical acceptance scenarios
text: KNOW-T10: Private sponsor investigation cannot be accessed by another partner through graph search, embeddings or exports.

heading: Critical acceptance scenarios
text: KNOW-T11: Direct charity correction is reviewed with original claim preserved.

heading: Critical acceptance scenarios
text: KNOW-T12: Replaying duplicate and out-of-order source updates yields identical canonical projection.

heading: Critical acceptance scenarios
text: KNOW-T13: Cross-language transliteration matches candidates but does not force an irreversible merge.

heading: Critical acceptance scenarios
text: KNOW-T14: A source parser changes field meaning; versioned definitions prevent silent corruption.

heading: Critical acceptance scenarios
text: KNOW-T15: An auditor recreates eligibility at the historical decision point using recorded-time and valid-time snapshots.

heading: Critical acceptance scenarios
text: KNOW-T16: A large source ingestion resumes after failure without duplicate evidence or skipped records.

heading: Decisions and research gates
text: KNOW-ADR-001: Strata capabilities for event history, ordering, bitemporal records and projections, verified experimentally.

heading: Decisions and research gates
text: KNOW-ADR-002: Semantic schema/ontology governance and F# compiler integration with echelon-knowledge-store.

heading: Decisions and research gates
text: KNOW-ADR-003: Entity resolution thresholds, human review capacity and quality targets.

heading: Decisions and research gates
text: KNOW-ADR-004: Rights policy enforcement for raw storage, derived claims, AI processing and API redistribution.

heading: Decisions and research gates
text: KNOW-ADR-005: Primary-source acquisition priority and verified dataset inventory, jurisdiction by jurisdiction.

heading: Decisions and research gates
text: KNOW-ADR-006: Common global public graph versus sponsor-private overlay, with data-sharing agreements.

heading: Decisions and research gates
text: KNOW-ADR-007: Retention/privacy reconciliation with append-only audit history.

heading: Decisions and research gates
text: KNOW-ADR-008: Freshness thresholds and legal source applicability by grant context.

heading: Decisions and research gates
text: KNOW-ADR-009: Performance, storage and acquisition cost budgets.

heading: Decisions and research gates
text: KNOW-ADR-010: Future external data product legal and commercial boundaries.

heading: Architecture decisions to resolve before implementation
text: - **ADR-001:** Verify Strata's actual persistence role and supported database engines, then select the managed database engine and true schema isolation capabilities; do not assume a specific provider.

heading: Architecture decisions to resolve before implementation
text: - **ADR-002:** Tenant registry and authorization provenance, including sponsor/partner relationships.

heading: Architecture decisions to resolve before implementation
text: - **ADR-003:** Connection pooling, schema binding, credential rotation, database role provisioning and SQL injection protections.

heading: Architecture decisions to resolve before implementation
text: - **ADR-004:** Event envelope, expected-version concurrency, idempotency index, ordering and outbox transaction.

heading: Architecture decisions to resolve before implementation
text: - **ADR-005:** Independently anchored integrity checkpoints and tenant-specific backup/restore.

heading: Architecture decisions to resolve before implementation
text: - **ADR-006:** Key management, PII vault and lawful erasure/retention across immutable events and backups.

heading: Architecture decisions to resolve before implementation
text: - **ADR-007:** Tenant migration fencing, dual-run validation, export and incident recovery.

heading: Architecture decisions to resolve before implementation
text: - **ADR-008:** EF Registry/Conditor compatible versions and deployment automation for managed infrastructure.

heading: Architecture decisions to resolve before implementation
text: - **ADR-009:** Partner isolation tier economics at 10/100/1,000 tenants.

heading: Architecture decisions to resolve before implementation
text: - **ADR-010:** Sponsor-level authoritative books and reporting when a sponsor serves multiple segregated partners.

heading: Enterprise and economic outcomes
text: - UNB-ENT-001: The enterprise SHALL express donor charitable intent as explicit goals, restrictions, and measurable outcomes independent of legacy forms.

heading: Enterprise and economic outcomes
text: - UNB-ENT-002: Every capability SHALL have an accountable owner, outcome metric, operating cost hypothesis, and documented alternative.

heading: Enterprise and economic outcomes
text: - UNB-ENT-003: The organization SHALL support a documented sponsor business model, revenue/fee policy, and sensitivity-tested unit economics.

heading: Enterprise and economic outcomes
text: - UNB-ENT-004: Enterprise operating decisions SHALL be explainable and reviewable without relying on an agent's private reasoning.

heading: Legal, authority and governance
text: - UNB-LEG-001: Every material legal assertion SHALL record jurisdiction, authoritative source, currency, interpretation, and review status.

heading: Legal, authority and governance
text: - UNB-LEG-002: The sponsor SHALL retain required legal ownership/control and final authority over distributions; donor recommendations SHALL not be treated as binding instructions.

heading: Legal, authority and governance
text: - UNB-LEG-003: The enterprise SHALL distinguish donor advice, sponsor decisions, operational execution, and audit evidence.

heading: Legal, authority and governance
text: - UNB-LEG-004: Conflicts, prohibited benefits, sanctions and other applicable restrictions SHALL have documented review and escalation paths, subject to jurisdiction-specific verification.

heading: Legal, authority and governance
text: - UNB-LEG-005: Changes to material policies SHALL be versioned, approved by authorized decision makers, and linked to impacted tests.

heading: Donor and grant outcomes
text: - UNB-DON-001: Donors SHALL be able to express charitable goals and recommendations in accessible channels without being forced into a single legacy workflow.

heading: Donor and grant outcomes
text: - UNB-DON-002: Contribution status SHALL be transparent while explicitly distinguishing pledged, received, valued, liquidated, and available funds.

heading: Donor and grant outcomes
text: - UNB-GRT-001: Every grant recommendation SHALL have a traceable eligibility determination, sponsor decision, execution state and reconciliation evidence.

heading: Donor and grant outcomes
text: - UNB-GRT-002: The enterprise SHALL handle incomplete, ambiguous, ineligible, disputed and potentially fraudulent recommendations safely.

heading: Donor and grant outcomes
text: - UNB-GRT-003: Charity due diligence SHALL be proportionate to documented risk and applicable requirements, with human escalation for exceptions.

heading: Assets, finance and advisors
text: - UNB-AST-001: The enterprise SHALL model cash, public securities and complex noncash contributions without pretending all assets settle identically.

heading: Assets, finance and advisors
text: - UNB-AST-002: Asset valuation, restrictions, custody state and liquidation SHALL have distinct, auditable records.

heading: Assets, finance and advisors
text: - UNB-FIN-001: All simulated financial events SHALL be recorded in balanced, immutable or correction-traceable accounting entries.

heading: Assets, finance and advisors
text: - UNB-FIN-002: Grants, fees, contributions and investment events SHALL reconcile to independent simulated statements; discrepancies SHALL block unsupported finality claims.

heading: Assets, finance and advisors
text: - UNB-ADV-001: Advisors SHALL operate only within explicit, revocable, scoped delegated permissions.

heading: Assets, finance and advisors
text: - UNB-ADV-002: Donor, advisor, sponsor and grantee roles SHALL have separately enforced access and information boundaries.

heading: AI, enterprise operations and technology
text: - UNB-AIO-001: Every agent action SHALL identify its permissions, inputs, policy version, result, evidence, and escalation route.

heading: AI, enterprise operations and technology
text: - UNB-AIO-002: High-impact, ambiguous, irreversible or legally reserved decisions SHALL require appropriate authorized human review.

heading: AI, enterprise operations and technology
text: - UNB-AIO-003: Agent unavailability, model changes and prompt injection SHALL not bypass deterministic financial or authorization controls.

heading: AI, enterprise operations and technology
text: - UNB-OPS-001: The enterprise SHALL support incident response, vendor failure, disputes, business continuity and recoverable audit trails.

heading: AI, enterprise operations and technology
text: - UNB-TEC-001: Integration SHALL use versioned contracts and the current Echelon Registry capability-discovery model; optional EF providers SHALL not break core operations.

heading: AI, enterprise operations and technology
text: - UNB-TEC-002: The intended implementation SHALL prioritize F#, WASM-first delivery, Limen and Forma where validated, managed persistence, and minimal operational complexity.

heading: AI, enterprise operations and technology
text: - UNB-TEC-003: Secrets, personal information and financial records SHALL have explicit classification, retention, access, and deletion policies.

heading: AI, enterprise operations and technology
text: - UNB-EXP-001: Every user journey SHALL be usable with keyboard, assistive technology, mobile layouts, and documented accessibility tests.

heading: AI, enterprise operations and technology
text: - UNB-EXP-002: Public identity SHALL be independently branded as Unbound, with transparent attribution to EF as its construction platform.

heading: AI, enterprise operations and technology
text: - UNB-VAL-001: Each requirement SHALL link to normal, exception and adversarial acceptance scenarios.

heading: AI, enterprise operations and technology
text: - UNB-VAL-002: Every claimed efficiency gain SHALL distinguish observed test measurements, modeled assumptions and unverified projections.

heading: AI, enterprise operations and technology
text: - UNB-VAL-003: The project SHALL log EF autonomous contributions, manual intervention, failures, cost, and reproducibility.

heading: Business outcome requirements (source: outcome-model.md O-01..O-18)

text: - UNB-LS-015: Support succession, inactivity, transfers, record export and portability (O-16).

heading: Business outcome requirements (source: outcome-model.md O-01..O-18)
text: - UNB-LS-016: Protect confidential donor, advisor and grantee information (O-17).

heading: Novel mechanism candidates: do not freeze these as mandatory solutions
text: - UNB-HYP-001: Continuous charity eligibility and diff-triggered rescreening may replace per-grant repetitive lookup. Measure false holds, missed changes, staleness and latency (INN-01/03/34).

heading: Novel mechanism candidates: do not freeze these as mandatory solutions
text: - UNB-HYP-002: Sponsor-approved policy-as-code and policy compiler with back-testing may eliminate routine manual approval work; require safe rollout, rollback, rule versioning and independent approval (INN-05/21).

heading: Novel mechanism candidates: do not freeze these as mandatory solutions
text: - UNB-HYP-003: Reusable, time-bounded determinations may reduce specialist effort; test invalidation, reuse factor and cross-sponsor legal/data rights (INN-04/02).

heading: Novel mechanism candidates: do not freeze these as mandatory solutions
text: - UNB-HYP-004: A shared grant state machine and grant identifier carried through remittance may improve recipient reconciliation (INN-08).

heading: Novel mechanism candidates: do not freeze these as mandatory solutions
text: - UNB-HYP-005: Continuous three-way reconciliation and event-ledger architecture may reduce break handling; test duplicated, missing, out-of-order and reversed events (INN-20/22/39).

heading: Novel mechanism candidates: do not freeze these as mandatory solutions
text: - UNB-HYP-006: Advisor-embedded DAF interaction and narrowly scoped delegations may reduce donor friction; prove explicit consent, revocation, sponsor control and integration economics (INN-15/26).

heading: Novel mechanism candidates: do not freeze these as mandatory solutions
text: - UNB-HYP-007: Sponsor-owned portable records and a documented transfer protocol may reduce lock-in; assess confidentiality, retention and interoperability (INN-17/18/44).

heading: Novel mechanism candidates: do not freeze these as mandatory solutions
text: - UNB-HYP-008: Recipient-side status and shared verification services may improve nonprofit experience; test cold-start, fraud and network governance (INN-07/38).

heading: Novel mechanism candidates: do not freeze these as mandatory solutions
text: - UNB-HYP-009: Donor-selected execution windows and spend-down horizons may improve operations and philanthropic outcomes; validate donor acceptance and avoid unauthorized delays or coercion (INN-37/19).

heading: Novel mechanism candidates: do not freeze these as mandatory solutions
text: - UNB-HYP-010: Shared policy packs and specialist decision-right routing may improve scaling; test correlated errors, credentialing and segregation of duties (INN-36/47).

heading: Commercial model requirements, not premature commitments
text: - UNB-COM-001: Evaluate sponsor model A (traditional enhanced), B (AI-native sponsor), C (infrastructure provider), D (partner sponsor-of-record), and Dc (captive sponsor) using common economics, legal risk, capital, evidence time, distribution and reversibility criteria.

heading: Commercial model requirements, not premature commitments
text: - UNB-COM-002: Preserve a capability architecture that can support C and D without making sponsor asset ownership a technical prerequisite.

heading: Commercial model requirements, not premature commitments
text: - UNB-COM-003: Require real customer discovery, executed data rights and measured pilot outcomes before asserting that C→D is commercially superior.

heading: Commercial model requirements, not premature commitments
text: - UNB-COM-004: Distinguish the **full synthetic sponsor reference enterprise** needed to demonstrate EF from the **commercial market-entry model**. The former does not decide the latter.

heading: Safety and control requirements
text: - UNB-CTL-001: Classify decisions as deterministic (D), probabilistic recommendation/flag (P), or human-authorized (H). P alone must not clear controls or move money.

heading: Safety and control requirements
text: - UNB-CTL-002: Donor/advisor/agent requests never become binding sponsor instructions without valid sponsor policy and authority.

heading: Safety and control requirements
text: - UNB-CTL-003: Every material capability has exactly one accountable human role even when its executor is automated.

heading: Safety and control requirements
text: - UNB-CTL-004: Cross-system business events must be idempotent, provenance-linked and correctable, with reconciliation before finality claims.

heading: Safety and control requirements
text: - UNB-CTL-005: Prohibit pay-first/verify-later, sampling that replaces legally necessary review, and model-only auto-clear approaches unless an independently reviewed lawful control design establishes otherwise.

heading: Safety and control requirements
text: - UNB-CTL-006: Model year-end surge, custodian outage, liquidity stress, vendor data restrictions and correlated AI failures.

heading: Capability coverage requirement
text: UNB-CAP-001: Every source capability C1.1–C6.4 SHALL map to an enterprise outcome, accountable human role, executor mode, control owner, interface boundary and acceptance scenarios. Six groups:

heading: Capability coverage requirement
text: UNB-CAP-002: Accountability and software execution SHALL be separate attributes; no automated executor eliminates the named human accountable for its capability.

heading: Capability coverage requirement
text: UNB-CAP-003: Legacy departmental handoffs, status inquiries and duplicate data entry SHALL be treated as avoidable failure mechanisms, not standalone capabilities.

heading: Capability coverage requirement
text: UNB-CAP-004: Each capability SHALL be classified as sponsor-specific, reusable infrastructure, shared service, or external dependency, with explicit tenant isolation and commercial packaging implications.

heading: Workflow outcome requirements
text: UNB-WF-001: Routine cash contribution through domestic grant (WF-01) SHALL trace settlement, acknowledgment, recommendation, sponsor authorization, payment and recipient evidence without unnecessary manual handoffs.

heading: Workflow outcome requirements
text: UNB-WF-002: Securities gifts (WF-02) SHALL distinguish transfer intent, orphan deposits, settlement, gift-date determination, valuation and booking.

heading: Workflow outcome requirements
text: UNB-WF-003: Complex noncash gifts (WF-03) SHALL require documented acceptance, specialist authority, valuation and tax/reporting checks.

heading: Workflow outcome requirements
text: UNB-WF-004: Cryptocurrency gifts (WF-04) SHALL use asset acceptance, chain/source-of-funds controls, custody and disposition states; eligibility is a policy/legal decision, not presumed.

heading: Workflow outcome requirements
text: UNB-WF-005: High-volume and recurring grants (WF-05) SHALL preserve idempotency, policy gates, liquidity, bounded fan-out and exception capacity under year-end surge.

heading: Workflow outcome requirements
text: UNB-WF-006: Foreign grants (WF-06) SHALL preserve equivalency/expenditure-responsibility review and sanctions controls where applicable.

heading: Workflow outcome requirements
text: UNB-WF-007: Domestic non-charity grants (WF-07) SHALL require appropriate expenditure-responsibility decisioning and records.

heading: Workflow outcome requirements
text: UNB-WF-008: Fiscal-sponsor grants (WF-08) SHALL resolve legal payee, project relationship, purpose restrictions and recipient evidence.

heading: Workflow outcome requirements
text: UNB-WF-009: Mid-flight eligibility changes (WF-09) SHALL trigger holds or controlled post-payment handling based on transaction state.

heading: Workflow outcome requirements
text: UNB-WF-010: Returns and payee-bank changes (WF-10) SHALL require payee integrity controls, independent confirmation where risk warrants, and reversible reconciliation.

heading: Workflow outcome requirements
text: UNB-WF-011: Donor AI agents (WF-11) SHALL act only within explicit scoped delegation and confirmation thresholds; requests never bypass sponsor authority.

heading: Workflow outcome requirements
text: UNB-WF-012: Advisor onboarding (WF-12) SHALL verify institution, individual authority, privileges, revocation and integration contracts.

heading: Workflow outcome requirements
text: UNB-WF-013: Donor death and succession (WF-13) SHALL handle document conflicts, authority transitions and dispute holds.

heading: Workflow outcome requirements
text: UNB-WF-014: Outbound transfer (WF-14) SHALL preserve history, restrictions, accounting reconciliation and sponsor approval.

heading: Workflow outcome requirements
text: UNB-WF-015: Dormant accounts (WF-15) SHALL follow approved notice, successor and charitable-default policies.

heading: Workflow outcome requirements
text: UNB-WF-016: Documentation requests (WF-16) SHALL produce accurate evidence-grounded documents with authorization and privacy controls.

heading: Workflow outcome requirements
text: UNB-WF-017: Liquidity shocks (WF-17) SHALL model available cash, market movements, custodian outages and approvals outside the playbook.

heading: Workflow outcome requirements
text: UNB-WF-018: NAV, unitization and fees (WF-18) SHALL track valuation inputs, pricing exceptions, effective schedules and corrections.

heading: Workflow outcome requirements
text: UNB-WF-019: Continuous reconciliation (WF-19) SHALL compare ledger, custodian, bank and payment-rail states, and escalate breaks.

heading: Workflow outcome requirements
text: UNB-WF-020: Continuous close and filings (WF-20) SHALL produce traceable reports and preserve accountable officer sign-off.

heading: Workflow outcome requirements
text: UNB-WF-021: State registration deadlines (WF-21) SHALL track applicability, changes, reminders and authorized submission.

heading: Workflow outcome requirements
text: UNB-WF-022: Regulatory change (WF-22) SHALL generate reviewed policy changes, back-tests, approval, canary and rollback evidence.

heading: Workflow outcome requirements
text: UNB-WF-023: Agent permission changes (WF-23) SHALL require independent evaluation and approval with explicit rollback.

heading: Workflow outcome requirements
text: UNB-WF-024: Board oversight (WF-24) SHALL separate reproducible evidence snapshots from interpretive commentary and preserve board authority.

heading: API and architectural requirements
text: UNB-API-001: Evaluate all 36 API domains against capability ownership and consumer needs before freezing interfaces.

heading: API and architectural requirements
text: UNB-API-002: Externally exposed writes SHALL express requests rather than grant approvals, money instructions, trades, direct ledger postings or policy publication.

heading: API and architectural requirements
text: UNB-API-003: A shared authorization model SHALL govern humans, institutions and agent principals; no borrowed credentials or self-escalation.

heading: API and architectural requirements
text: UNB-API-004: Mutating commands SHALL have idempotency, concurrency handling, evidence references and stable machine-readable errors.

heading: API and architectural requirements
text: UNB-API-005: Tenant boundaries SHALL prevent cross-sponsor personal-data exposure; explicitly shared data must have separate rights and provenance.

heading: API and architectural requirements
text: UNB-API-006: External partner events SHALL be signed, replay-safe, deduplicated and traceable to authoritative states.

heading: API and architectural requirements
text: UNB-API-007: Favor one F# modular monolith with clear internal capability boundaries; API-first SHALL NOT imply microservices-first. This remains subject to EF current-version compatibility review.

heading: API and architectural requirements
text: UNB-API-008: Treat the five illustrative OpenAPI documents as design references, not verified production contracts; defer implementation until requirements approval.

heading: Agent authority requirements
text: UNB-AGT-001: Map AG-01..AG-19 to the current EF agent catalog, deduplicating roles and distinguishing deterministic jobs from actual agents.

heading: Agent authority requirements
text: UNB-AGT-002: AI agents may read scoped information, propose, flag, draft or open cases; they SHALL NOT independently clear flags, write authoritative records, instruct payments/trades or approve their own output.

heading: Agent authority requirements
text: UNB-AGT-003: Tool broker enforcement SHALL remove prohibited tools rather than rely on prompts.

heading: Agent authority requirements
text: UNB-AGT-004: The eight source invariants INV-A1..INV-A8 SHALL be translated to explicit negative and property tests, including approval actor type, flag clearance, payment gate, delegation confirmation, segregation of duties and agent-chain quarantine.

heading: Agent authority requirements
text: UNB-AGT-005: Policy/rule decisions and human decisions SHALL be independently identifiable, versioned and auditable.

heading: Governing conversion requirements
text: - **UNB-TRACE-001:** Every source event below SHALL receive an Unbound event contract with immutable event ID, event/effective/recorded times, authorized producer, schema version, causation, provenance, correction/supersession semantics, idempotency, replay safety and side-effect classification. Event rows marked as money-capable require a separately verified sponsor decision and payment/trade gate.

heading: Governing conversion requirements
text: - **UNB-TRACE-002:** Every source control below SHALL be mapped to one or more requirements, applicable regulatory assertions or documented operational risks, control owner, preventive/detective class, objective evidence and executable failure test. The source control catalog is a candidate control baseline, not proof of control operation.

heading: Governing conversion requirements
text: - **UNB-TRACE-003:** Every REG row below SHALL be evaluated for source authority, law/guidance/proposal distinction, current status, jurisdiction, sponsor-versus-provider applicability and qualified reviewer approval. A legal assertion without a reviewed control/evidence mapping SHALL block regulatory readiness.

heading: Governing conversion requirements
text: - **UNB-TRACE-004:** Every source scenario below SHALL be converted into a testable normal, exceptional, adversarial or recovery case with detect, contain, escalate, correct, evidence and residual risk. Correction is always append-only; simulation shall verify prior states remain reconstructible.

heading: Governing conversion requirements
text: - **UNB-TRACE-005:** No source architecture target, financial assumption or legal interpretation is considered validated merely because a CSV row exists. Record evidence maturity and independent reproduction.

text: - **UNB-REGMAP-001:** Maintain a machine-checkable, one-row-per-REG applicability register with primary citation, accessed date, jurisdiction, affected entity, effective date, classification, accountable reviewer, source evidence and status.

heading: Append-only database acceptance specification
text: - **UNB-IMM-001:** An authorized append transaction creates an immutable authoritative event and durable sequence position. All existing authoritative event bytes remain unchanged; reject UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE and destructive schema migration through normal operational roles.

heading: Append-only database acceptance specification
text: - **UNB-IMM-002:** A correction must specify target event/record, reason, actor, effective time, recorded time, evidence and correction kind. Reject an orphan correction and preserve the original in all audit queries.

heading: Append-only database acceptance specification
text: - **UNB-IMM-003:** Ledger corrections use append-only balanced reversal plus replacement or adjustment. No destructive balance reset.

heading: Append-only database acceptance specification
text: - **UNB-IMM-004:** Historical queries support (a) actual effective date and (b) what was known by recorded date. A backdated correction does not retroactively alter an earlier as-known view.

heading: Append-only database acceptance specification
text: - **UNB-IMM-005:** Deterministic projection rebuild from an immutable snapshot/checkpoint and subsequent events produces the same state as full replay. Snapshot is a cache, never authority.

heading: Append-only database acceptance specification
text: - **UNB-IMM-006:** Replays do not issue external effects. Durable effect receipts and external idempotency keys prevent double grants, payments, trades, notices and filings.

heading: Append-only database acceptance specification
text: - **UNB-IMM-007:** Detect missing, tampered, reordered and duplicated records; demonstrate independent checkpoint verification and restore without accepting a silently truncated history.

heading: Append-only database acceptance specification
text: - **UNB-IMM-008:** A privacy or retention request is handled through an approved policy preserving legally required evidence while honoring applicable rights. Do not claim cryptographic erasure works if plaintext exists in backups, logs or exports.

heading: Append-only database acceptance specification
text: - **UNB-IMM-009:** Cross-tenant authorization is enforced for event append, projection, historical replay, export and correction. Test attempted cross-tenant corrections and provenance leakage.

heading: Append-only database acceptance specification
text: - **UNB-IMM-010:** Require load tests for 10× grant surge, historical replay and projection rebuild at defined scales; measure storage, integrity verification and correction propagation costs before selecting storage technology.

heading: Explicit deferral: outbound payments
text: - **UNB-PAY-001:** Model grant sponsor approval, accounting recognition, payment obligation, payment instruction, payment authorization, submission, acceptance, settlement, return, void, recovery and reconciliation as separate events.

heading: Explicit deferral: outbound payments
text: - **UNB-PAY-002:** Define a provider-neutral payment API and lifecycle, accommodating ACH, wires, checks and other approved rails subject to eligibility, geography, contracts and sponsor policy.

heading: Explicit deferral: outbound payments
text: - **UNB-PAY-003:** No grant recommendation, AI proposal or internal accounting journal directly authorizes outbound funds. Enforce sponsor reserved authority, independent release control, payee verification and least privilege.

heading: Explicit deferral: outbound payments
text: - **UNB-PAY-004:** Require idempotent external instructions, replay defense, duplicate detection, settlement evidence, reconciliation, safe retry and explicit uncertain-result handling.

heading: Explicit deferral: outbound payments
text: - **UNB-PAY-005:** Record immutable payee identity, bank detail change controls, sanctions/eligibility freshness, approval evidence, payment status and correction/recovery history, with appropriate secrets/privacy protection.

heading: Explicit deferral: outbound payments
text: - **UNB-PAY-006:** Support bank/rail outages, failed transfers, returned ACH, lost/voided checks, partial payments, payment holds, escheat/unclaimed property applicability and fraud escalation.

heading: Explicit deferral: outbound payments
text: - **UNB-PAY-007:** Provide a simulated payment adapter and deterministic contract tests for grant/accounting integration before any real funds can move.

heading: Explicit deferral: outbound payments
text: - **UNB-PAY-008:** Payment provider selection, sponsor bank relationships, funds-flow legal review, rail eligibility, limits, fraud operations, security certification and production authorization are explicit future decision gates.

heading: Explicit deferral: outbound payments
text: - **UNB-PAY-009:** Forma SHALL display pending/approved/sent/settled/failed/returned states without conflating them. Folio SHALL generate payment advice, remittance notices and reconciliation/audit packs.

heading: Explicit deferral: outbound payments
text: - **UNB-PAY-010:** Payment events SHALL reconcile grant payable, sponsor cash, custodian liquidity and bank confirmation, without claiming a payment is complete before external confirmation.

heading: Cross-domain failure scenarios (required executable acceptance specifications)
text: - **UNB-XSC-001:** Grant funded from three investments; one redemption fails, another settles late and third NAV is corrected after charity payment. Preserve settled payment, compute correction impacts, enforce liquidity and authorized compensations.

heading: Cross-domain failure scenarios (required executable acceptance specifications)
text: - **UNB-XSC-002:** Simultaneous advisors submit percentage grants against the same fund; price shifts and reservations cannot create excess obligations.

heading: Cross-domain failure scenarios (required executable acceptance specifications)
text: - **UNB-XSC-003:** Sponsor employee revocation occurs during an approved but not executed custody transfer; authority is rechecked at execution.

heading: Cross-domain failure scenarios (required executable acceptance specifications)
text: - **UNB-XSC-004:** Donor death during unsettled investment transfer and pending grant; succession and sponsor authority determine each pending action.

heading: Cross-domain failure scenarios (required executable acceptance specifications)
text: - **UNB-XSC-005:** Partner migration between schema/database isolation tiers during active close; no duplicate postings, cross-tenant exposure or missing source evidence.

heading: Cross-domain failure scenarios (required executable acceptance specifications)
text: - **UNB-XSC-006:** A custodian statement conflicts with pool NAV, a grant is pending and an AI proposes an override; deterministic controls hold affected actions until independent review.

heading: Cross-domain failure scenarios (required executable acceptance specifications)

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-001:** Provide a complete configurable, versioned chart of accounts with legal entity, sponsor, partner/program, DAF fund, department, project, restriction, asset, currency and other approved reporting dimensions; enforce dimension validity.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-002:** All accounting postings SHALL be double-entry, balanced by defined accounting entity and currency/measurement rules, with immutable journal headers/lines, unique posting IDs, effective dates, recorded dates, authorizers and provenance.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-003:** Posted journals SHALL never be updated or deleted. Corrections SHALL use linked reversal, adjustment or reclassification entries with approval and preserved original history.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-004:** Maintain integrated general ledger and subsidiary ledgers for DAF balances, cash/banks, custody/securities, grants payable, accounts payable, accounts receivable, contributions, investments, fees, expenses, payroll interface, fixed assets where relevant and inter-entity balances.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-005:** Separate donor-advised fund accounting from sponsor operating activity and enforce restrictions, liquidity and sponsor ownership/control; DAF subfund balances are not personally owned donor assets.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-006:** Record contribution lifecycle from intent through receipt, valuation, restrictions, acceptance, acknowledgment, settlement and disposition, with distinct cash, securities and complex noncash treatments.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-007:** Record grant lifecycle from recommendation through sponsor approval, commitment, payable, payment, clearing, returns, voids and recoveries; no recommendation alone creates a payment.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-008:** Support cash, accrual and required reporting bases through explicit approved policies and reconciled adjustments; do not assume a single basis applies to every entity/report.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-009:** Support investments, units/NAV, gains/losses, interest, dividends, corporate actions, custody reconciliation, valuations, impairments and liquidity, subject to documented accounting policy.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-010:** Support sponsor and partner fee schedules, accruals, waivers, allocations, revenue recognition, billing, collections and intercompany/interfund settlement without double counting.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-011:** Support internal fund allocations, fund mergers, closures, outbound transfers, successor-account splits and multigenerational successor transfers with balanced immutable entries, restrictions and provenance.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-012:** Support accounts payable, purchasing/expense approvals, vendor master controls, reimbursements, accruals, prepaid expenses and payment reconciliation for sponsor operations.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-013:** Support accounts receivable, invoicing, credit adjustments, collections and deferred revenue where applicable.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-014:** Support budgeting, forecasts, actual-versus-budget reporting, cost centers, allocation methodologies and scenario models while distinguishing forecasts from posted actuals.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-015:** Support multiple legal entities and sponsor structures, intercompany/interfund transactions, eliminations and consolidated reporting where authorized and legally applicable.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-016:** Support currencies, FX rates, source currency, functional/reporting currency, remeasurement, translation and realized/unrealized FX results where needed; currency conversion never silently changes source amounts.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-017:** Define accounting periods, soft/hard close, reconciliations, close checklists, adjusting entries, period locks, reopen approvals and late-arriving event treatment without modifying posted journals.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-018:** Reconcile GL and subledgers to independent bank, custodian, payment-rail, investment and partner statements, with aged breaks, ownership, evidence and escalation.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-019:** Provide financial statements including trial balance, balance sheet/statement of financial position, statement of activities, cash flows, functional expenses where required, fund statements, restricted/unrestricted analyses and management reporting, subject to entity-specific reporting rules.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-020:** Support audit schedules, roll-forwards, supporting workpapers, transaction drill-down, external auditor access, evidence export and independently verifiable as-of financial snapshots.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-021:** Support tax and regulatory reporting source data, including applicable Form 990/DAF disclosures and other filings, with jurisdictional applicability and human sign-off; do not assume automatic filing authority.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-022:** Enforce segregation of duties for journal preparation, approval, posting, bank/payee changes, reconciliations, close certification, master data and payment release; AI cannot approve its own accounting actions.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-023:** Every accounting operation SHALL have an authenticated, versioned API with authorization, idempotency, concurrency, error states, traceability and evidence; external callers cannot directly post unrestricted journals or instruct money movement.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-024:** Forma SHALL provide accessible mobile-first accounting experiences, including approval, exceptions, fund statements, reconciliation review, close dashboards and audit drill-down; complex tasks must remain possible on a phone.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-025:** Folio SHALL generate accessible versioned financial statements, fund statements, acknowledgments, reconciliations, audit packages and regulator-ready human-readable reports with source/policy/template provenance.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-026:** Strata integration SHALL preserve immutable posting, correction links, temporal queries, tenant isolation, replay-safe projections and integrity checks; gaps in verified Strata functionality are blockers or require governed companion components.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-027:** Partner segregation SHALL apply to every journal, account, dimension, bank connection, projection, statement, export and AI accounting context, supporting separate schemas, databases and dedicated infrastructure.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-028:** Define controlled accounting imports/exports, partner ERP integrations, banking feeds and custodian feeds; external systems can be reconciliation sources without silently replacing Unbound's authoritative books.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-029:** Implement deterministic posting rules and policy-versioned accounting treatments; AI may propose classification and journal drafts but cannot bypass posting, approval or reconciliation controls.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-030:** Financial integrity invariants SHALL be continuously checkable: balanced journals, valid dimensions, nonduplicated external effects, reconciled control accounts, authorized allocations, preserved restrictions and no unauthorized negative available balance.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-031:** Support tax-lot and cost-basis tracking where relevant, with donor tax acknowledgment values distinguished from sponsor accounting basis, proceeds and valuation.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-032:** Model pledges, conditional gifts, restricted contributions, contingent liabilities and commitments separately from settled available assets, using applicable accounting policies.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-033:** Support nonprofit accounting classifications and net assets with/without donor restrictions where applicable; avoid conflating donor-advised subfund designation with legally donor-restricted net assets.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-034:** Support configurable fiscal years, reporting calendars, accrual schedules, scheduled allocations, recurring journals and authorized close automation with safe retries.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-035:** Support fraud detection, unusual-journal review, duplicate invoice/payee detection, anomalous transfers, break aging, financial control attestations and independently reviewable AI signals.

heading: Core accounting requirements
text: - **UNB-ACC-036:** Establish performance and recoverability requirements for high-volume posting, year-end grant surges, long historical ledgers, tenant migration, backup/restore and deterministic projection rebuild.

heading: Candidate requirements
text: - **UNB-PART-001:** A fund SHALL support an arbitrary number of participant-to-fund relationships, subject only to explicit, versioned sponsor policy and operational limits, not schema or UI cardinality.

heading: Candidate requirements
text: - **UNB-PART-002:** A person or organization SHALL be able to participate in multiple funds, each with independent scoped roles and permissions.

heading: Candidate requirements
text: - **UNB-PART-003:** Relationships SHALL distinguish contributor/donor, original advisor, additional advisor, authorized viewer, administrative contact, professional advisor, successor advisor, successor-designate, and sponsor staff; these are independently assignable and may overlap.

heading: Candidate requirements
text: - **UNB-PART-004:** Every relationship SHALL record its own effective period, recorded time, source of authority, grantor, scope, expiry, revocation and verification state. Changes append events; no in-place mutation.

heading: Candidate requirements
text: - **UNB-PART-005:** The fund SHALL support multiple concurrent recommendation-makers with separately scoped permissions; sponsor-approved policy SHALL resolve conflicts, simultaneous recommendations, limits and revocation.

heading: Candidate requirements
text: - **UNB-PART-006:** Access and communications SHALL be role- and relationship-specific; adding a participant does not automatically grant access to other participants' personal data, contribution history, or unrelated funds.

heading: Candidate requirements
text: - **UNB-PART-007:** Onboarding SHALL support invitation, acceptance, identity verification, declined invitation, inactive status and removal without deleting history.

heading: Candidate requirements
text: - **UNB-PART-008:** Fund governance SHALL support configurable consent and approval patterns where permitted (individual recommendation, joint consent, designated lead, sponsor review), without representing donor voting as binding sponsor control.

heading: Candidate requirements
text: - **UNB-PART-009:** The experience SHALL support many participants accessibly on mobile, including search, grouping, delegated administration, clear permissions and conflict explanation.

heading: Successor account requirements
text: - **UNB-SUCC-001:** A fund SHALL support a versioned succession plan with zero, one or many designated successors, priority/order, conditions, contingencies, activation triggers and sponsor approval status.

heading: Successor account requirements
text: - **UNB-SUCC-002:** Succession SHALL distinguish **continuing the original fund with successor advisory privileges** from **creating one or more distinct successor DAF accounts** under sponsor-approved policy.

heading: Successor account requirements
text: - **UNB-SUCC-003:** A successor DAF account SHALL have a distinct fund identifier, sponsor/program association, its own participant/privilege graph, policy, reporting and accounting projections, and an immutable link to the originating fund and succession decision.

heading: Successor account requirements
text: - **UNB-SUCC-004:** A succession plan MAY specify fractional or amount-based allocations to multiple successor accounts, subject to approved minimums, restrictions, liquidity and valuation rules. Allocations must be deterministic, auditable and reconcile exactly; no assumed automatic division.

heading: Successor account requirements
text: - **UNB-SUCC-005:** Succession SHALL support successive generations, successor-of-successor designations, substitute/contingent successors and configurable generation or time limits defined by sponsor policy.

heading: Successor account requirements
text: - **UNB-SUCC-006:** Triggers MAY include verified death, incapacity, resignation, expiration, and other sponsor-defined events. Allegations alone SHALL NOT automatically activate privileges or transfer assets.

heading: Successor account requirements
text: - **UNB-SUCC-007:** The system SHALL handle contested documents, inconsistent instructions, simultaneous deaths, unavailable or ineligible successors, minors, incapacitated successors, and no surviving designee through holds and authorized human resolution.

heading: Successor account requirements
text: - **UNB-SUCC-008:** Succession activation SHALL atomically or recoverably suspend/revoke former advisory authority, establish successor permissions, enforce open-grant and standing-instruction policies, and preserve pending commitments and restrictions.

heading: Successor account requirements
text: - **UNB-SUCC-009:** Successor account allocations SHALL use append-only balanced internal fund allocation entries, referencing the original and new accounts, sponsor decision, valuation basis, and effective/recorded times. No direct mutation of prior balances or history.

heading: Successor account requirements
text: - **UNB-SUCC-010:** Donor/advisor-facing succession planning SHALL explain that a DAF is not personally owned or inherited, and that sponsor approval and program rules govern any successor account or advisory designation.

heading: Successor account requirements
text: - **UNB-SUCC-011:** The system SHALL support sponsor-approved charitable beneficiaries or spend-down instructions when no successor account is created, without conflating these with private beneficiaries.

heading: Successor account requirements
text: - **UNB-SUCC-012:** Every activation, dispute, amendment, allocation, reversal and correction SHALL be represented by immutable authoritative records; reconstruction must answer what instructions and evidence were known at any point.

heading: Successor account requirements
text: - **UNB-SUCC-013:** A succession plan SHALL be previewable as a graph or allocation simulation showing successors, fallback paths, restrictions, account minimums and potential conflicts before approval.

heading: Successor account requirements
text: - **UNB-SUCC-014:** Succession and successor-account creation SHALL be tenant-scoped and policy-governed, including transfers between sponsor programs and any cross-sponsor case; never assume cross-sponsor portability is automatic.

heading: Mandatory requirements
text: - **UNB-TEN-001:** Every partner SHALL have an immutable tenant identity independent of database name, schema name, hostname and infrastructure location.

heading: Mandatory requirements
text: - **UNB-TEN-002:** Support shared-database/separate-schema, dedicated-database, and dedicated-infrastructure deployment profiles through explicit configuration and validated compatibility; partner business logic must not fork by tier.

heading: Mandatory requirements
text: - **UNB-TEN-003:** Every authoritative event, fund, party relationship, grant, journal entry, policy, evidence reference, agent action and projection SHALL have an enforced tenant security boundary. Cross-tenant access is denied by default, including administrator, background job, support, analytics and agent paths.

heading: Mandatory requirements
text: - **UNB-TEN-004:** Tenant routing SHALL derive from verified identity and authorized tenancy context, never a client-supplied schema/database name or unverified header. Use an independently tested routing and connection-broker boundary.

heading: Mandatory requirements
text: - **UNB-TEN-005:** For shared databases with separate schemas, partner-specific roles SHALL be unable to read/write other schemas; default schema search paths, SECURITY DEFINER routines, migrations, connection pooling, shared extensions and administrative credentials require threat modeling and negative tests.

heading: Mandatory requirements
text: - **UNB-TEN-006:** For dedicated databases, credentials, encryption keys, backup/restore policy, resource quotas, monitoring, recovery objectives and access reviews SHALL be partner-scoped to the degree promised by contract.

heading: Mandatory requirements
text: - **UNB-TEN-007:** Shared services (identity, registry, charity intelligence, orchestration, telemetry, support and model services) SHALL have an explicit classification: shared public reference, permitted aggregated information, partner-confidential information, or prohibited cross-tenant flow. Shared infrastructure must not become an unreviewed data-sharing mechanism.

heading: Mandatory requirements
text: - **UNB-TEN-008:** Support per-partner retention, residency, encryption-key management, privacy policy, audit export, disaster recovery objectives, data processing agreements and access restrictions where technically and legally applicable.

heading: Mandatory requirements
text: - **UNB-TEN-009:** Tenant isolation SHALL apply to caches, queues, event streams, outboxes, object storage, search indexes, backups, logs, observability, prompt/context construction, embeddings, evaluation datasets and generated documents, not just relational tables.

heading: Mandatory requirements
text: - **UNB-TEN-010:** Partner-specific policies and configurations SHALL be versioned immutable records with sponsor/partner authority boundaries; a partner's preferences cannot override the sponsoring charity's reserved legal authority.

heading: Mandatory requirements
text: - **UNB-TEN-011:** Tenant provisioning, migration, upgrade, suspension and offboarding SHALL use a governed, reproducible plan with approvals, inventory, integrity verification, rollback/compensation strategy and evidence.

heading: Mandatory requirements
text: - **UNB-TEN-012:** Migrate a tenant between isolation profiles without changing stable tenant/fund/party/event identifiers or losing append-only provenance, corrections, balances, policy versions, consent, grants, audit chain or bitemporal reconstruction.

heading: Mandatory requirements
text: - **UNB-TEN-013:** Migration SHALL use a consistent event high-water mark, verifiable source/destination record equivalence, independent ledger reconciliation, replay-safe outbox handoff and controlled cutover. Never permit two active authoritative writers for one tenant.

heading: Mandatory requirements
text: - **UNB-TEN-014:** Backups and restoration SHALL honor tenant boundaries. A shared physical backup does not guarantee independent per-tenant recovery; document and test tenant-selective restore and confidentiality limitations.

heading: Mandatory requirements
text: - **UNB-TEN-015:** Define explicit partner-specific performance, availability, recovery and capacity targets. Shared-schema tiers must have noisy-neighbor detection and isolation controls.

heading: Mandatory requirements
text: - **UNB-TEN-016:** Each partner SHALL have an exportable, evidence-complete logical dataset and portability protocol, subject to lawful retention, sponsor ownership, third-party rights and contracts.

heading: Mandatory requirements
text: - **UNB-TEN-017:** Operations SHALL record which isolation profile and security controls were in effect for a partner at any point in time; changes are append-only authorized events.

heading: Mandatory requirements
text: - **UNB-TEN-018:** Before selecting a database engine, benchmark schema counts, migration fan-out, connection pools, query planner/locking contention, event replay, integrity checking, tenant restore and cost at realistic partner sizes.

heading: Mandatory requirements
text: - **UNB-TEN-019:** Unbound's F# modular monolith and managed database preference SHALL remain compatible with per-tenant connection routing. A multi-database deployment does not require a microservices architecture.

heading: Mandatory requirements
text: - **UNB-TEN-020:** Multi-sponsor, multi-partner and multi-fund are separate dimensions. Model sponsor legal entity, distribution partner, institutional channel, and DAF account distinctly; a partner is not automatically the legal sponsor, and one sponsor may serve several partners.

heading: Non-negotiable platform requirements
text: - **UNB-PLAT-001:** All business capabilities SHALL expose governed, versioned APIs/contracts, including internal capability boundaries. API-first does not require microservices; F# modular monolith remains preferred.

heading: Non-negotiable platform requirements
text: - **UNB-PLAT-002:** All application user interfaces SHALL use **Forma** and the approved Echelon design system. Do not introduce alternate UI frameworks without an explicit documented exception approved by the owner.

heading: Non-negotiable platform requirements
text: - **UNB-PLAT-003:** All enterprise-generated documents, printable statements, acknowledgments, grant correspondence, reports and export-ready human-readable artifacts SHALL use **Folio** where technically supported. Validate Folio's actual rendering, accessibility and archival capabilities before asserting compliance.

heading: Non-negotiable platform requirements
text: - **UNB-PLAT-004:** Every interactive user journey SHALL be **mobile-first**, including donor, joint-advisor, successor, sponsor, compliance, partner and administrative experiences. A phone must support essential completion, not just viewing.

heading: Non-negotiable platform requirements
text: - **UNB-PLAT-005:** Accessibility SHALL be designed and tested to **WCAG 2.2 Level AA** as a measurable baseline, plus applicable ADA and other jurisdiction-specific legal obligations. Passing automated WCAG checks alone does not establish ADA legal compliance.

heading: Non-negotiable platform requirements
text: - **UNB-PLAT-006:** The backend SHALL be F# and WASM-first UI integration SHALL use current compatible Echelon components, including Limen and Forma, subject to Registry/Conditor verification. No unapproved alternate runtime/framework.

heading: Non-negotiable platform requirements
text: - **UNB-PLAT-007:** **Strata** SHALL be used in the persistence architecture. All authoritative business history is append-only; corrections and reversals append new records. Physical storage guarantees and Strata integration must be verified.

heading: Non-negotiable platform requirements
text: - **UNB-PLAT-008:** Partner data isolation SHALL support separate schemas, separate databases and dedicated infrastructure, selected per partner; all shared services must preserve tenant boundaries.

heading: Non-negotiable platform requirements
text: - **UNB-PLAT-009:** Forma and Folio SHALL use a coherent branded design system, consistent content semantics, typography, color contrast, error patterns and accessibility tokens; each public-facing application has a nonblank loading experience and clear independent identity.

heading: API contract standard
text: - **UNB-API-STD-001:** Every API defines caller roles, sponsor authority boundary, request/response schemas, validation, version, idempotency, optimistic concurrency where relevant, privacy classification, authorization policy, error codes and audit evidence.

heading: API contract standard
text: - **UNB-API-STD-002:** Every state-changing API defines accepted/requested versus approved/executed states, async completion, retry rules, cancellation and compensation, and a documented side-effect boundary.

heading: API contract standard
text: - **UNB-API-STD-003:** All APIs and event contracts require backward compatibility strategy, deprecation policy, schema evolution, contract tests, tracing/correlation IDs, rate limits and explicit failure behavior.

heading: API contract standard
text: - **UNB-API-STD-004:** External APIs cannot directly approve sponsor-reserved decisions, initiate money movement, modify authoritative events or grant privileges outside governed approval boundaries.

heading: API contract standard
text: - **UNB-API-STD-005:** Every integration documents authentication method, credential rotation, least privilege, webhook signature verification, replay defense, partner context binding, provider outage behavior and test fixtures.

heading: API contract standard
text: - **UNB-API-STD-006:** API descriptions SHALL be generated from or verified against authoritative contracts, with no undocumented implementation-only business operations.

heading: Forma interaction and mobile standard
text: - **UNB-UX-001:** Each essential task SHALL have a phone-sized reference flow, including multi-party participation, successor planning, grant recommendation, account statements, sponsor review and exceptions.

heading: Forma interaction and mobile standard
text: - **UNB-UX-002:** Forms, dialogs, focus, validation, navigation, errors, tables, graphs and notifications SHALL support keyboard and assistive technology; equivalent nonvisual alternatives required for visual succession graphs.

heading: Forma interaction and mobile standard
text: - **UNB-UX-003:** Interfaces SHALL expose pending, completed, blocked, failed and uncertain states distinctly; never imply a recommendation was approved or a payment completed when only requested.

heading: Forma interaction and mobile standard
text: - **UNB-UX-004:** Slow network, interrupted session, duplicate tap, stale state, expired delegation and offline/poor connectivity SHALL have safe recovery patterns.

heading: Forma interaction and mobile standard
text: - **UNB-UX-005:** Test zoom/reflow, text spacing, contrast, touch target sizing, screen-reader announcements, focus order, error identification and reduced-motion behavior on supported mobile and desktop platforms.

heading: Forma interaction and mobile standard
text: - **UNB-UX-006:** Accessibility testing SHALL include automated checks, keyboard-only operation, manual screen-reader review, and representative assistive-technology task completion, with documented defects and retests.

heading: Forma interaction and mobile standard
text: - **UNB-UX-007:** Avoid exposing internal EF tool names or implementation concepts in donor-facing experiences unless genuinely relevant to the user.

heading: Folio and evidence standard
text: - **UNB-DOC-001:** Each generated document SHALL retain source event/version references, effective and recorded times, template version, policy version, generation timestamp, authorizing actor and integrity metadata.

heading: Folio and evidence standard
text: - **UNB-DOC-002:** Statements and acknowledgments SHALL distinguish source evidence, corrections and as-of dates; regeneration must not silently rewrite historical delivered documents.

heading: Folio and evidence standard
text: - **UNB-DOC-003:** Folio outputs SHALL be tested for accessibility, legibility, mobile preview, printing, archival/export requirements and multilingual/locale formatting where supported.

heading: Folio and evidence standard
text: - **UNB-DOC-004:** Document delivery SHALL be role-scoped and tenant-isolated, with immutable delivery receipts, privacy-safe notifications and controlled redaction.

heading: Folio and evidence standard
text: - **UNB-DOC-005:** Templates and document-generation APIs SHALL be versioned, tested against synthetic fixtures, and resistant to untrusted content injection.

heading: AI, resilience and governance standard
text: - **UNB-AI-STD-001:** Agent actions SHALL use the same governed APIs and tenant-scoped authorization as humans; no database shortcuts or privileged hidden tools.

heading: AI, resilience and governance standard
text: - **UNB-AI-STD-002:** Evidence, uncertainty, model/prompt version, policy version and authorized human sign-off SHALL be captured for material AI-assisted decisions.

heading: AI, resilience and governance standard
text: - **UNB-AI-STD-003:** Deterministic controls govern money, access, eligibility gates and policy publication; agents may not self-approve or clear their own alerts.

heading: AI, resilience and governance standard
text: - **UNB-RES-001:** Each critical capability SHALL define failure modes for model, database, partner API, custodian, payment rail, document renderer and identity provider outages.

heading: AI, resilience and governance standard
text: - **UNB-RES-002:** Replay and recovery SHALL not duplicate external payments, grants, trades, messages or account allocations; test idempotency and single-writer fencing.

heading: AI, resilience and governance standard
text: - **UNB-RES-003:** Every capability SHALL have defined RTO/RPO, service ownership, operational runbooks, telemetry, incident escalation and recovery validation proportionate to criticality.

heading: 1. Accounting boundaries and invariants
text: - ACC-MDL-001: Define legal entity, partner, program, internal fund, account, currency, period, restriction, counterparty, asset/security, custody account, transaction source, event ID and posting-policy version independently. Every posted line has valid required dimensions.

heading: 1. Accounting boundaries and invariants
text: - ACC-MDL-002: Authoritative journals are strictly append-only. A correction is a new reversal/reclassification/adjustment with explicit linkage, reason, evidence, authorization and bitemporal dates; no update/delete of posted entries.

heading: 1. Accounting boundaries and invariants
text: - ACC-MDL-003: Every journal balances in its defined book, currency and accounting basis. Multicurrency postings must balance in transaction and functional currencies under an approved FX methodology; never pretend two unlike currencies can be summed.

heading: 1. Accounting boundaries and invariants
text: - ACC-MDL-004: Distinguish cash/assets held, fund net asset balances, available-to-recommend amounts, grant commitments, legally restricted net assets, and operational reserves. Available-to-recommend is a controlled projection, **not a general-ledger account**.

heading: 1. Accounting boundaries and invariants
text: - ACC-MDL-005: Enforce fund/account authorization and restrictions at posting and query boundaries, and tenant isolation across schemas, databases, agents, caches and exports.

heading: 1. Accounting boundaries and invariants
text: - ACC-MDL-006: Every business event maps to zero or more authorized journals under a versioned posting policy. Some events (recommendations, invitations, plan approvals) are **nonposting**; posting requires a separate recognized accounting trigger.

heading: 1. Accounting boundaries and invariants
text: - ACC-MDL-007: Posting is idempotent per event, accounting book and posting-rule version, with explicit treatment of restatements; event replay must not create duplicate journals or external effects.

heading: 1. Accounting boundaries and invariants
text: - ACC-MDL-008: Separate financial statement classification from fund advisory designation and reporting dimensions. Accounting-policy review must determine donor restriction classification; DAF subfund designation does not automatically imply donor-restricted net assets.

heading: 1. Accounting boundaries and invariants
text: - ACC-MDL-009: Control accounts reconcile to detailed subsidiary ledgers and independent bank/custody/payment evidence; unbalanced or unexplained breaks block unsupported close certifications.

heading: 1. Accounting boundaries and invariants
text: - ACC-MDL-010: Closed periods remain immutable. Late discoveries are recognized through authorized subsequent-period adjustments and/or formally approved comparative restatement, with preserved originally issued statements.

heading: 1. Accounting boundaries and invariants
text: - ACC-MDL-011: Use Strata in the approved persistence architecture; validate actual capabilities before mapping event store, journals, projections and integrity enforcement to Strata.

heading: 1. Accounting boundaries and invariants
text: - ACC-MDL-012: APIs are the only governed application command surface; Forma handles accessible mobile-first accounting operations; Folio produces traceable, versioned financial and fund reports.

heading: 9. Decision register before final posting rules
text: ACC-ADR-001: Authoritative accounting framework and qualified nonprofit accountant review (US GAAP/other).

heading: 9. Decision register before final posting rules
text: ACC-ADR-002: Sponsor/legal-entity topology and whether fund accounting is one GL with dimensions or balanced subledgers.

heading: 9. Decision register before final posting rules
text: ACC-ADR-003: Contribution recognition timing, conditional promises, complex gifts and valuation policy.

heading: 9. Decision register before final posting rules
text: ACC-ADR-004: Grant expense/payable recognition timing and conditional grants.

heading: 9. Decision register before final posting rules
text: ACC-ADR-005: Investment valuation, units/NAV, lot basis and realized/unrealized reporting.

heading: 9. Decision register before final posting rules
text: ACC-ADR-006: Internal fee recognition, cost recovery, interfund balancing and consolidated eliminations.

heading: 9. Decision register before final posting rules
text: ACC-ADR-007: Restrictions vs internal DAF designation; available-to-recommend calculation.

heading: 9. Decision register before final posting rules
text: ACC-ADR-008: Strata verified transaction, append-only, integrity and projection capabilities.

heading: 9. Decision register before final posting rules
text: ACC-ADR-009: Multi-currency, FX, settlement and legal-entity consolidation.

heading: 9. Decision register before final posting rules
text: ACC-ADR-010: Partner schema/database isolation, sponsor-wide consolidated reporting and access control.

heading: 9. Decision register before final posting rules
text: ACC-ADR-011: Close, period locks, late adjustments and restatement policy.

heading: 9. Decision register before final posting rules
text: ACC-ADR-012: Tax/reporting support and external accountant/auditor sign-off.
