heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-001:** Define a custodian-neutral adapter contract for account registration, identity mapping, account status, positions, cash, transactions, prices, tax lots where available, corporate actions, fees, transfers, statements, reconciliation and exceptions.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-002:** Support multiple custodians per sponsor, partner, program and DAF, with multiple custody accounts per DAF and explicit legal ownership/account title, restrictions, account purpose and authorization.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-003:** Support custody account opening and maintenance through documented provider-specific capabilities; where APIs are unavailable, define governed file/manual exception channels without claiming end-to-end automation.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-004:** Define normalized investment account, instrument/security, position, lot, trade, settlement, cash movement, income, corporate action, price, valuation, fee and statement schemas, retaining raw source evidence and provider identifiers.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-005:** Support read-only holdings and transaction feeds independently of trade execution. Never infer that a provider supporting balances also permits trading, transfer initiation or account opening.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-006:** Define explicit investment authority: sponsor policy, investment committee, authorized manager, discretionary mandate, account-level permissions, trading limits, prohibited assets, concentration and liquidity controls.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-007:** Trade recommendations, orders, approvals, submission, acceptance, execution, partial fill, cancellation, rejection and settlement SHALL be distinct states. Execution APIs require separately validated contractual permissions and human authority.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-008:** Cash transfers, withdrawals, wires, ACH and securities transfers SHALL use independent authorization, payee/beneficiary verification, separation of duties, limits, reconciliation and provider-specific settlement evidence.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-009:** Support scheduled polling, provider webhooks where available, batch files, secure statements and exception ingestion, with signed/verifiable origin, freshness, deduplication, ordering and replay protection.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-010:** Reconcile custodian positions, transactions, cash, valuations and fees to Unbound's investment subledger, GL, bank/payment evidence and fund available-to-recommend calculation.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-011:** Reconciliation exceptions SHALL capture missing trades, orphan deposits, stale prices, mismatched quantities, delayed settlement, rejected transfers, corporate actions, duplicate records and unresolved balances.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-012:** External provider facts SHALL be appended with source, as-of time, received time, normalization version, hash and confidence/status. Corrections append superseding facts; no mutation of authoritative history.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-013:** Apply Strata-backed append-only persistence requirements and tenant isolation to custody data, authorization, raw files, normalized events, ledger postings, outbox, credentials and audit evidence.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-014:** Support advisor-managed accounts, model portfolios, sponsor-approved investment pools, managed portfolios and self-directed recommendations only where program policy and provider contracts permit.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-015:** Model liquidity and unsettled proceeds separately from settled spendable cash; grant approval and payment gating must account for market movement, restrictions and settlement risk.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-016:** Corporate actions, distributions, splits, reorganizations, fees, dividends, interest and realized/unrealized gains must have deterministic posting rules and independent reconciliation.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-017:** Support provider-specific authentication, scoped credentials, key rotation, secure transport, rate limits, service accounts, incident response, data licensing and entitlement verification.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-018:** Provide a partner- and sponsor-aware integration registry recording each provider's verified capability matrix, data freshness, connection status, authority, contract, sandbox, service-level objectives and operational owner.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-019:** Partner isolation SHALL hold even when the same custodian serves multiple partners. Never use a provider account identifier alone as a global security boundary.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-020:** Forma SHALL provide mobile-first accessible portfolio views, holdings, cash availability, trade/request states, discrepancies, investment mandates and approvals with clear source freshness.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-021:** Folio SHALL produce custody reconciliation packs, fund investment statements, portfolio activity reports, manager oversight reports and audit-ready documents with immutable source/provenance references.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-022:** Custodian outages, delayed feeds, revoked permissions, malformed files and account freezes SHALL trigger defined degraded modes, holds, freshness warnings and escalation without inventing balances or executing unsafe transfers.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-023:** Custodian migrations and advisor changes SHALL preserve complete immutable history, account mappings, tax lots where available, open orders, restrictions, settlements and authorized successor-account allocations.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-024:** Integrations SHALL support synthetic fixtures and provider sandboxes where available, contract tests, negative authorization tests, replay/idempotency tests, reconciliation tests and recovery drills before production authorization.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-025:** Document contractual boundaries for asset custody, investment discretion, trade execution, valuation reliance, fiduciary oversight, privacy, incident liability, statement of record and record retention.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-026:** Custodian adapter contracts SHALL be versioned APIs independent of vendor-specific implementation. Core fund accounting and grant workflows shall not require a particular custodian.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-027:** Model investment performance, benchmarks, time-weighted/money-weighted returns and manager attribution with explicit calculation methods and source limitations; distinguish performance reports from accounting valuations.

heading: Required capabilities
text: - **UNB-CUST-028:** Support fund-level and sponsor-level exposure/portfolio aggregation only with authorized access and correct look-through/beneficial-accounting semantics; no unintended cross-partner leakage.

heading: Account structure requirements
text: - **UNB-INV-001:** Model legal sponsor, legal account holder, custodian, custody account, portfolio, investment pool, internal DAF fund, subfund position, investment mandate and manager as distinct identities with effective-dated relationships.

heading: Account structure requirements
text: - **UNB-INV-002:** Support a DAF mapped to one or many segregated custody accounts, and one custody account supporting multiple DAFs via explicitly governed omnibus allocation.

heading: Account structure requirements
text: - **UNB-INV-003:** Support pooled investment vehicles with fund-level units/shares, valuation dates, unit prices, subscriptions, redemptions, rounding, cash buffers and participant-level holdings.

heading: Account structure requirements
text: - **UNB-INV-004:** Sponsor-wide pool totals SHALL reconcile to custody assets and fund-level units; every subscription/redemption must have balanced, append-only accounting effects.

heading: Account structure requirements
text: - **UNB-INV-005:** Support DAF allocation among approved portfolios/pools with minimums, eligibility, restrictions, target percentages, rebalancing rules and effective dates.

heading: Account structure requirements
text: - **UNB-INV-006:** Support separately managed accounts and external advisors/RIA relationships with explicit investment discretion, delegated scope, account identifiers, limits, expiry and revocation.

heading: Account structure requirements
text: - **UNB-INV-007:** Support model portfolios as versioned target allocation specifications, separate from actual holdings and separately from executable trade instructions.

heading: Account structure requirements
text: - **UNB-INV-008:** Model account structures and migrations as sponsor-approved, auditable changes; no loss of source custody identifiers, tax lots, historical valuations or reconciliation evidence.

heading: Account structure requirements
text: - **UNB-INV-009:** Support multiple custodians and multiple asset managers simultaneously, including manager transitions and overlapping read-only reporting periods.

heading: Account structure requirements
text: - **UNB-INV-010:** Sponsor can configure allowable structures by partner, program, DAF type, account size, asset class, jurisdiction and legal/contractual eligibility.

heading: Account structure requirements
text: - **UNB-INV-011:** Do not infer that a donor-specific custody account is legally donor-owned or that pooled units are legally transferable securities; document actual legal and accounting classification.

heading: Account structure requirements
text: - **UNB-INV-012:** Support in-kind contribution and in-kind transfer workflows, including asset acceptance, restrictions, valuation, liquidation policy and custody settlement.

heading: Authority, preferences and policy
text: - **UNB-INV-013:** Donor/advisor investment preferences SHALL be modeled as recommendations or policy-permitted elections, not automatically as trade authority.

heading: Authority, preferences and policy
text: - **UNB-INV-014:** Sponsor policy SHALL define investment menus, prohibited investments, ESG/mission preferences where supported, liquidity thresholds, concentration limits, rebalancing tolerance, manager eligibility and exception escalation.

heading: Authority, preferences and policy
text: - **UNB-INV-015:** Every portfolio change distinguishes request, policy evaluation, sponsor decision, approved instruction, execution, settlement and reconciliation.

heading: Authority, preferences and policy
text: - **UNB-INV-016:** Delegated investment discretion SHALL be explicit, time-bound where appropriate, auditable, revocable and restricted to named legal accounts/mandates.

heading: Authority, preferences and policy
text: - **UNB-INV-017:** Multiple participants with conflicting preferences SHALL follow a documented fund governance rule; no last-write-wins overwrite of approved policy.

heading: Authority, preferences and policy
text: - **UNB-INV-018:** Sponsor can freeze trading or allocation changes for compliance holds, donor death/incapacity, disputed succession, valuation uncertainty, liquidity stress or custodian outage.

heading: Authority, preferences and policy
text: - **UNB-INV-019:** AI may recommend portfolios, risk checks, liquidity plans and rebalancing, but may not bypass sponsor approval, mandate boundaries, suitability review where applicable, or execution controls.

heading: Authority, preferences and policy
text: - **UNB-INV-020:** Investment policies and exceptions SHALL be versioned, effective-dated and linked to event, decision, account and reporting evidence.

heading: Valuation, unitization and accounting
text: - **UNB-INV-021:** Define valuation methodology per asset class and investment structure, including market prices, stale pricing, illiquid assets, corporate actions and manual valuation approval.

heading: Valuation, unitization and accounting
text: - **UNB-INV-022:** Pool unit prices SHALL derive from an approved NAV calculation with documented assets, liabilities, fees, valuation time, cutoffs, rounding and exception policy.

heading: Valuation, unitization and accounting
text: - **UNB-INV-023:** Define subscriptions/redemptions using explicit trade date, valuation date, settlement date and recorded date; reject unsupported backdating and preserve bitemporal corrections.

heading: Valuation, unitization and accounting
text: - **UNB-INV-024:** Distinguish settled cash, pending trades, unsettled proceeds, encumbered liquidity, grants payable, reserved commitments and available-to-recommend balance.

heading: Valuation, unitization and accounting
text: - **UNB-INV-025:** Define investment gains/losses, income, dividends, fees, management expenses, FX and tax-lot/cost-basis treatment in versioned deterministic posting rules.

heading: Valuation, unitization and accounting
text: - **UNB-INV-026:** For segregated accounts, reconcile each legal custody account to DAF investment subledger and sponsor GL. For omnibus/pools, reconcile custody -> pool NAV -> units -> DAF holdings -> sponsor GL.

heading: Valuation, unitization and accounting
text: - **UNB-INV-027:** Unit allocations, fee allocations and performance calculations SHALL be reproducible from immutable events and policy versions; corrections append and trigger controlled revaluation/reissue.

heading: Valuation, unitization and accounting
text: - **UNB-INV-028:** Performance reports SHALL specify time-weighted versus money-weighted return methodology, benchmarks, cash-flow treatment, fees and as-of dates; do not equate accounting gain with performance return.

heading: Valuation, unitization and accounting
text: - **UNB-INV-029:** Define rounding residuals and break thresholds so unit balances, NAV and fund totals reconcile deterministically.

heading: Valuation, unitization and accounting
text: - **UNB-INV-030:** Define liquidity planning for grant commitments and stress scenarios; no investment recommendation may imply that unsettled or illiquid assets are immediately spendable.

heading: Portfolio operations and integrations
text: - **UNB-INV-031:** Support policy-governed rebalance proposals, drift detection, manager reviews, trade staging, restricted lists, pretrade controls and posttrade compliance.

heading: Portfolio operations and integrations
text: - **UNB-INV-032:** Investment order routing is optional per custodian entitlement. Read-only feeds, file imports, manager-managed execution and API execution are separate capability profiles.

heading: Portfolio operations and integrations
text: - **UNB-INV-033:** Each custodian/manager integration SHALL declare verified entitlements, account scope, data freshness, order authority, reconciliation sources, failure modes and contractual restrictions.

heading: Portfolio operations and integrations
text: - **UNB-INV-034:** Support transfers between segregated accounts and pools with explicit sale/transfer, valuation, fees, tax lots, settlement and sponsor approvals; never assume a book transfer moves external assets.

heading: Portfolio operations and integrations
text: - **UNB-INV-035:** Support investment restrictions and grant-related liquidity holds across multi-custodian, multi-pool portfolios without oversubscription or double counting.

heading: Portfolio operations and integrations
text: - **UNB-INV-036:** Support investment manager fee schedules, pool-level fees, DAF-level charges, waivers and sponsor fee recovery with no double counting in consolidated financial reporting.

heading: Portfolio operations and integrations
text: - **UNB-INV-037:** Support custody/manager failures, stale feeds, failed settlement, halted trading, valuation dispute, market closures, liquidity gates and suspended pool redemptions through explicit degraded states.

heading: Portfolio operations and integrations
text: - **UNB-INV-038:** All investment APIs SHALL be versioned, tenant-bound, authorization-scoped and idempotent for external effects, with append-only evidence and safe retries.

heading: Portfolio operations and integrations
text: - **UNB-INV-039:** Forma SHALL provide accessible mobile-first portfolio overview, investment preferences, risk/return context, allocation, liquidity, manager oversight and exceptions with source freshness.

heading: Portfolio operations and integrations
text: - **UNB-INV-040:** Folio SHALL produce reproducible, accessible investment statements, NAV reports, manager reviews, policy exception reports and fund allocation reports with source/provenance metadata.

heading: Portfolio operations and integrations
text: - **UNB-INV-041:** Partner segregation SHALL cover custody mapping, model portfolios, pool units, pricing, mandates, manager access, derived analytics, documents and AI context.

heading: Portfolio operations and integrations
text: - **UNB-INV-042:** Strata-backed immutable records SHALL support custody observations, approved mandates, portfolio decisions, unit transactions, valuation snapshots, corrections and reconciliation events, subject to verified Strata capabilities.

heading: Binding invariants
text: - **UNB-NAV-001:** Every investment pool has an accounting entity, sponsor, pool ID, functional currency, valuation policy/version, approved calendar/cutoff, custodian mappings and effective-dated eligible DAFs.

heading: Binding invariants
text: - **UNB-NAV-002:** Every authoritative source observation, NAV run, price, unit transaction, allocation, adjustment, approval and publication is append-only. Corrections append linked superseding records, never UPDATE/DELETE.

heading: Binding invariants
text: - **UNB-NAV-003:** Calculate NAV deterministically from eligible assets less liabilities, using approved pricing sources, cutoff, accounting basis, accrued income, fees, expenses, unsettled trades and FX policies. Never treat missing prices as zero without explicit approved policy.

heading: Binding invariants
text: - **UNB-NAV-004:** Unit price = NAV attributable to outstanding units / outstanding units, with approved treatment for first issuance, zero units, negative NAV, suspended valuation and residuals.

heading: Binding invariants
text: - **UNB-NAV-005:** Valuation states SHALL distinguish Draft, InputsValidated, Calculated, ExceptionHold, IndependentlyReviewed, Approved, Published, Corrected/Superseded and Rejected; publishing is a controlled act, not a calculation side effect.

heading: Binding invariants
text: - **UNB-NAV-006:** A valuation SHALL have immutable source high-water marks, as-of/effective time, recorded time, price-source versions, FX rates, posting policy, rounding policy, code/rule version, reviewer and integrity checkpoint.

heading: Binding invariants
text: - **UNB-NAV-007:** Validate custodian cash/positions, security identifiers, quantities, corporate actions, liabilities, accrued fees, unrecognized items and interfund allocations before publication; material unexplained breaks prevent final publication.

heading: Binding invariants
text: - **UNB-NAV-008:** Define independent maker-checker approval for published NAV and privileged overrides; AI may propose resolutions but cannot approve its own calculations or overrides.

heading: Binding invariants
text: - **UNB-NAV-009:** Support daily, periodic and event-driven valuations, with explicit calendars, market closures, holidays, valuation freezes and after-cutoff processing.

heading: Binding invariants
text: - **UNB-NAV-010:** Every published valuation and dependent report must remain reproducible as originally issued, even after a correction.

heading: Binding invariants
text: - **UNB-NAV-011:** Define separate calculated NAV, approved NAV, published NAV and currently effective NAV; API consumers must explicitly request the intended view.

heading: Binding invariants
text: - **UNB-NAV-012:** Pool and DAF unit positions, liability allocations and GL balances SHALL reconcile under an approved tolerance/rounding policy; no unexplained balancing plug.

heading: Pricing and valuation
text: - **UNB-NAV-013:** Define pricing hierarchy by asset class: independent market feed, custodian mark, approved valuation service, documented manual appraisal, or explicit hold. Source precedence and freshness limits are policy controlled.

heading: Pricing and valuation
text: - **UNB-NAV-014:** Support securities, cash, funds, fixed income, illiquid assets, restricted holdings, accrued interest/dividends, corporate actions and currencies where allowed by investment policy.

heading: Pricing and valuation
text: - **UNB-NAV-015:** Stale, conflicting, missing or outlier prices create exceptions with severity, affected assets/funds, fallback candidates and reviewer decision; never silently forward-fill.

heading: Pricing and valuation
text: - **UNB-NAV-016:** FX valuation retains original currency, quote time, rate source, conversion method and functional currency; distinguish FX remeasurement from investment performance.

heading: Pricing and valuation
text: - **UNB-NAV-017:** Illiquid valuations require appraisal methodology, approval, uncertainty range where meaningful, age limits and valuation-event triggers; mark provisional if policy permits.

heading: Pricing and valuation
text: - **UNB-NAV-018:** Pricing corrections must trigger impact analysis across NAV, units, fees, grants, financial statements and manager performance, not only change the displayed price.

heading: Pricing and valuation
text: - **UNB-NAV-019:** A provider observation is evidence, not automatically an approved accounting mark; reconcile source conflicts explicitly.

heading: Unitization, subscriptions and redemptions
text: - **UNB-NAV-020:** Each pool subscription/redemption has fund, pool, amount or units, requested/approved/accepted timestamps, valuation point, cutoff decision, fees, settlement and external/internal transfer references.

heading: Unitization, subscriptions and redemptions
text: - **UNB-NAV-021:** Define forward-pricing or other approved allocation methodology explicitly. Do not allow a participant or agent to choose a known favorable historical unit price.

heading: Unitization, subscriptions and redemptions
text: - **UNB-NAV-022:** Use fixed-precision decimal/rational arithmetic with specified precision, rounding mode and residual allocation. Never binary floating point for authoritative monetary/unit calculations.

heading: Unitization, subscriptions and redemptions
text: - **UNB-NAV-023:** Unit issuance = accepted net subscription amount / applicable approved unit price, subject to rounding, minimum unit increment and residual handling.

heading: Unitization, subscriptions and redemptions
text: - **UNB-NAV-024:** Redemption proceeds = approved redeemed units × applicable approved unit price, less applicable charges, subject to settlement, cash availability, gating and rounding policy.

heading: Unitization, subscriptions and redemptions
text: - **UNB-NAV-025:** Pending subscriptions and redemptions SHALL not change outstanding units before the policy-defined recognition/strike point; avoid circular NAV calculations.

heading: Unitization, subscriptions and redemptions
text: - **UNB-NAV-026:** Partial redemptions, gates, suspensions, insufficient units, restricted allocations and unsettled transfers require explicit state and deterministic handling.

heading: Unitization, subscriptions and redemptions
text: - **UNB-NAV-027:** Every unit issue/redeem/transfer preserves sponsor-wide pool totals and has balanced fund subledger and GL posting rules; custody movements are tracked separately from internal allocation.

heading: Unitization, subscriptions and redemptions
text: - **UNB-NAV-028:** Prevent oversubscription, duplicate processing and simultaneous redemption races through idempotency, optimistic concurrency/single-writer controls and fund-level reservations.

heading: Unitization, subscriptions and redemptions
text: - **UNB-NAV-029:** A DAF may hold multiple pool positions and separate custody positions; portfolio aggregation must avoid double counting underlying pooled holdings.

heading: Unitization, subscriptions and redemptions
text: - **UNB-NAV-030:** Successor-account splits and DAF mergers preserve total units, restrictions, commitments and audit history; fractional rounding residuals require explicit policy.

heading: Unitization, subscriptions and redemptions
text: - **UNB-NAV-031:** Pool closure, merger, share-class change and migration require governed conversion ratios, notices, approvals and reproducible allocations.

heading: Fees, performance and liquidity
text: - **UNB-NAV-032:** Support sponsor, manager, custodian, investment pool and performance-related fees only where policy/contract permits, with explicit assessment base, accrual frequency, tiers, minimums, waivers and effective dates.

heading: Fees, performance and liquidity
text: - **UNB-NAV-033:** Accrue liabilities before NAV strike when required by approved policy; ensure fees are not charged twice at pool and DAF levels.

heading: Fees, performance and liquidity
text: - **UNB-NAV-034:** Define distribution/income reinvestment, fund-level allocation and realized/unrealized gain treatment independently of unit price changes.

heading: Fees, performance and liquidity
text: - **UNB-NAV-035:** Distinguish total NAV, settled cash, unsettled cash, encumbered cash, redemption proceeds pending, grant commitments and available-to-recommend funds.

heading: Fees, performance and liquidity
text: - **UNB-NAV-036:** Support liquidity buffers, redemption gates, side pockets if approved, market halts and stress tests; do not promise immediate cash from illiquid holdings.

heading: Fees, performance and liquidity
text: - **UNB-NAV-037:** Performance metrics define TWR/MWR method, benchmark, gross/net fees, cash-flow timing and valuation assumptions; NAV growth alone is not a valid return measure.

heading: Corrections, replay and financial close
text: - **UNB-NAV-038:** Corrected NAV is a new approved publication linked to the original, with cause, affected period, affected pool/funds, materiality, responsible reviewer and downstream remediation plan.

heading: Corrections, replay and financial close
text: - **UNB-NAV-039:** Corrections distinguish source-price error, missed position, late trade, corporate action, FX error, fee accrual error, wrong cutoff, unit allocation error and fraud/unauthorized override.

heading: Corrections, replay and financial close
text: - **UNB-NAV-040:** Calculate counterfactual units and monetary impacts for each affected fund, transaction, grant, fee, statement and period; preserve original and corrected views.

heading: Corrections, replay and financial close
text: - **UNB-NAV-041:** Apply a sponsor-approved materiality/remediation policy, including when to compensate affected funds, restate NAV, adjust units, issue corrected statements or escalate to auditor/regulator.

heading: Corrections, replay and financial close
text: - **UNB-NAV-042:** Never retroactively overwrite settled transfers or historical unit issuance. Append corrective journals/unit events, reconcile to original and approved revised economic outcomes.

heading: Corrections, replay and financial close
text: - **UNB-NAV-043:** Closed-period corrections require separate accounting-close and restatement authority; originally published Folio reports and their delivery receipts remain preserved.

heading: Corrections, replay and financial close
text: - **UNB-NAV-044:** Rebuild projections from append-only Strata-integrated evidence deterministically and compare checksums, units, balances and published results.

heading: Corrections, replay and financial close
text: - **UNB-NAV-045:** Correction propagation must be idempotent and bounded, with explicit causal dependencies, impact report, approval gate and no unbounded automated cascade.

heading: Corrections, replay and financial close
text: - **UNB-NAV-046:** If source facts or approvals are unavailable, valuation remains on hold or clearly provisional under policy; no fabricated NAV, prices, balances or completed settlements.

heading: Interfaces and enterprise integration
text: - **UNB-NAV-047:** Provide governed versioned APIs for pool setup, pricing observations, valuations, approval, publication, subscription, redemption, fee accrual, corrections, impact analysis, reconciliations and as-of queries.

heading: Interfaces and enterprise integration
text: - **UNB-NAV-048:** All APIs enforce sponsor/partner/fund/manager authority, tenant context, idempotency, immutable evidence and contract tests. No privileged bypass for AI.

heading: Interfaces and enterprise integration
text: - **UNB-NAV-049:** Forma provides mobile-first WCAG 2.2 AA-targeted accessible NAV review, price exceptions, pool positions, subscriptions, redemptions, correction impact, approvals and fund statements.

heading: Interfaces and enterprise integration
text: - **UNB-NAV-050:** Folio produces immutable-versioned pool valuation packs, DAF investment statements, fee disclosures, NAV correction notices, reconciliation evidence and auditor workpapers.

heading: Interfaces and enterprise integration
text: - **UNB-NAV-051:** Strata's actual transactional, append-only, ordering, projection and recovery capabilities must be verified; implement necessary companion guarantees only through approved architecture.

heading: Interfaces and enterprise integration
text: - **UNB-NAV-052:** All pricing, units, positions, NAV, evidence, reports and AI retrieval obey partner isolation across shared schemas, separate databases and dedicated infrastructure.

heading: Interfaces and enterprise integration
text: - **UNB-NAV-053:** Independent custody and bank data reconciliation is required; provider feed availability and data freshness are displayed rather than inferred.

heading: Deterministic acceptance tests
text: NAV-T01: NAV = eligible assets minus recognized liabilities with explicit inclusion/exclusion and no hidden balancing entries.

heading: Deterministic acceptance tests
text: NAV-T02: Zero units, zero/negative NAV, missing price, missing FX and stale custody feed enter defined safe states.

heading: Deterministic acceptance tests
text: NAV-T03: Price-source precedence, age limits, exceptions and manual overrides are reproducible.

heading: Deterministic acceptance tests
text: NAV-T04: Decimal precision, rounding, residual allocation and multiple sequential subscriptions reconcile.

heading: Deterministic acceptance tests
text: NAV-T05: Two subscriptions at same cutoff and a late submission use correct approved valuation point.

heading: Deterministic acceptance tests
text: NAV-T06: Duplicate/replayed subscription and redemption do not create duplicate units or cash movement.

heading: Deterministic acceptance tests
text: NAV-T07: Concurrent redemptions cannot exceed fund units, liquidity or sponsor limits.

heading: Deterministic acceptance tests
text: NAV-T08: Partial redemption/gating/market closure preserve requested, approved, executed and settled states.

heading: Deterministic acceptance tests
text: NAV-T09: Fee accrual reduces NAV correctly and is not charged twice.

heading: Deterministic acceptance tests
text: NAV-T10: Corporate action, late trade and FX correction trigger correct impact analysis and approved remediation.

heading: Deterministic acceptance tests
text: NAV-T11: Original NAV and Folio statement remain reproducible after corrected publication.

heading: Deterministic acceptance tests
text: NAV-T12: Successor split 50/30/20 preserves total units and restrictions within rounding policy.

heading: Deterministic acceptance tests
text: NAV-T13: Pool NAV, unit allocations, custody positions and GL reconcile or generate controlled breaks.

heading: Deterministic acceptance tests
text: NAV-T14: Closed-period correction retains original reports and creates authorized restatement artifacts.

heading: Deterministic acceptance tests
text: NAV-T15: Cross-partner unauthorized price/units/statement queries are denied across all isolation profiles.

heading: Deterministic acceptance tests
text: NAV-T16: An AI-proposed valuation override cannot publish without independent approval.

heading: Deterministic acceptance tests
text: NAV-T17: Strata-backed projection rebuild yields identical as-of results and integrity checkpoints.

heading: Deterministic acceptance tests
text: NAV-T18: Custodian outage and restart cannot publish stale NAV as current or duplicate postings.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-01 Missing or incomplete input:** Request minimal evidence; park task without inventing defaults.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-02 False or contradictory input:** Preserve source claims, detect conflict and escalate material ambiguity.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-03 Stale external data:** Label freshness, reevaluate applicability and block consequential decisions where required.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-04 Identity mismatch:** Hold permissions and sensitive actions until verified.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-05 Authority revoked mid-flight:** Cancel or suspend pending actions; reconcile any committed effects.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-06 Policy or law changes:** Version applicability, reassess affected decisions and seek qualified review.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-07 Agent hallucination:** Require source verification and independent decision gates.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-08 Prompt injection:** Ignore untrusted instructions, record attempt and isolate tool authority.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-09 Conflicting agents:** Create discrepancy with evidence, no silent consensus.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-10 External service outage:** Circuit break, queue safely, show degraded status and retry within bounds.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-11 Timeout with unknown outcome:** Reconcile using idempotency/correlation before retry.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-12 Duplicate delivery:** Deduplicate commands and notifications; preserve delivery evidence.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-13 Partial multi-step success:** Identify committed effects and compensate by authorized correction.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-14 Concurrent workflow collision:** Detect optimistic version conflicts and coordinate ownership.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-15 Tenant or scope leakage:** Deny, contain, audit and escalate privacy/security incident.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-16 Evidence collector failure:** Independent heartbeat and missing-evidence deficiency.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-17 Accounting or custody mismatch:** Hold dependent decisions and independently reconcile.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-18 Recipient eligibility drift:** Reevaluate before approval and execution, preserve prior decision.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-19 Approval invalidated by mutation:** Require renewed authorization on material change.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-20 Human reviewer unavailable:** Reassign through approved delegation and preserve deadline.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-21 Compensating control expires:** Enforce fail-closed or approved continuity route.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-22 Accessibility task failure:** Provide equivalent alternative and track usability defect.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-23 Widget host compromise:** Revoke embed grant and contain scoped exposure.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-24 Unsafe or misleading notification:** Suppress sensitive content, revoke recipient access and remediate.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-25 Audit export inconsistency:** Block publication until snapshot and denominator reconcile.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-26 Live payment attempt:** Deny; outbound live execution remains deferred.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-27 Recovery replays stale command:** Reauthorize and reevaluate before resumption.

heading: Initial fault taxonomy
text: - **FM-28 Unknown unknown / unclassified event:** Default to bounded safe state, open incident and learn through governed change.

heading: 2. Relationship rules
text: | ONT-1 | Party ≠ relationship ≠ authority. A person may be donor, advisor, successor and employee at once. Each capacity is a separate edge with its own evidence (PARTY-04). |

heading: 2. Relationship rules
text: | ONT-2 | A household or family group is presentation only. It confers no access (PARTY-05, SVC-06). |

heading: 2. Relationship rules
text: | ONT-3 | A fund relates to ≥1 legal entity, ≥0 custody accounts, ≥0 pools. Many-to-many with pools is normal (unitized pooled investing). |

heading: 2. Relationship rules
text: | ONT-4 | Every grant references exactly one fund. A grant from several funds is several grants (avoids ambiguous restriction and reservation semantics). Proposed [P]. |

heading: 2. Relationship rules
text: | ONT-5 | A recipient may be several legal identities over time (merger, EIN change). Identity changes create a new identity edge. They never rewrite past grants (admin scenario 12). |

heading: 2. Relationship rules
text: | ONT-6 | Channel (portal, widget, API, agent, staff entry) is an attribute of a request. It is never an entity with authority. |

heading: 0. Cross-cutting rules
text: | SM-0 | Terminal states reject ordinary commands. Later facts about a terminal object (return, refund, restatement, discovered ineligibility) create a **linked child record** with its own lifecycle. They never reopen or edit the parent. | Baseline WF-01 makes `Reconciled` terminal, yet returns, custodian corrections and post-payment reviews can arrive after it ([TVF-004](../16-registers/findings.csv)). |

heading: 0. Cross-cutting rules
text: | SM-1 | Every transition records: actor (person, rule ID or model run), authority reference, policy version, input snapshot hash, effective time, recorded time, causation ID. | Baseline DATA-03, data model principle 3. |

heading: 0. Cross-cutting rules
text: | SM-2 | Every command carries an expected revision. A stale revision is rejected, never merged silently. | Baseline financial core command envelope. |

heading: 0. Cross-cutting rules
text: | SM-3 | A transition that depends on an external party has an explicit **Unknown** state. Timeout never maps to failure. | Financial core invariant 7. Missing from the baseline grant machine ([TVF-003](../16-registers/findings.csv)). |

heading: 0. Cross-cutting rules
text: | SM-4 | Holds are *orthogonal flags*, not states. An object can be `Approved` and `Held`. A hold blocks forward transitions that move money or legal state. It never blocks cancellation, investigation or recording external observations. | The baseline mixes "Held" as a state (financial core lifecycle) and as a flag (WF-09). As a state, a hold erases where the object was. |

heading: 0. Cross-cutting rules
text: | SM-5 | A hold can be added by any authorized rule, person or model (flag-only, DD-005). It can be released only by a rule whose inputs have changed or by an authorized human. A model never releases. | DD-005. |

heading: 0. Cross-cutting rules
text: | SM-6 | Irreversible transitions (payment submission, trade submission, acknowledgment issuance, successor activation) re-check authority, eligibility, holds and data freshness **at the moment of the transition**, not at the earlier decision. | AUTH-06; WF-09 revocation between approval and payment. |

heading: 1. Grant recommendation (donor/advisor side)
text: | REC-1 | A recommendation never moves money and never reserves capacity. It may create a **soft pending claim** that lowers the *displayed* recommendable amount for the same fund. A soft claim has no financial effect. |

heading: 1. Grant recommendation (donor/advisor side)
text: | REC-2 | `Withdrawn` is allowed only before `DecisionIssued`. After approval, the requester can only *ask* for cancellation; the sponsor decides (Grant §2). |

heading: 1. Grant recommendation (donor/advisor side)
text: | REC-3 | A recommendation is attributed to: requesting principal, acting principal (for an agent or delegate), capacity, authority revision. If the requesting principal's authority ends before decision, the recommendation goes to `Submitted+AuthorityLapsed` review. It is not decided under authority that no longer exists. |

heading: 1. Grant recommendation (donor/advisor side)
text: | REC-4 | Duplicate detection is a flag, never a silent merge. Two identical recommendations from two advisors are two requests. |

heading: 1. Grant recommendation (donor/advisor side)
text: | REC-5 | Withdrawal or supersession closes the linked grant (`Withdrawn`) in the same operation. A specialist cannot approve a grant nobody is recommending (TVF-089). |

heading: 1. Grant recommendation (donor/advisor side)
text: | REC-6 | A recurring template instance has the idempotency key (template, period). The missed-run policy (catch up or skip) is stated per template [P]. Template amendment and resumption follow REC-3 authority checks. An agent-created template requires the principal's confirmation at creation and at each amendment (TVF-095, TVF-098). |

heading: 1. Grant recommendation (donor/advisor side)
text: | REC-7 | **Delayed execution re-confirms.** A pre-cleared plan item (giving plan, alternative 2D) or a recurring instance whose recipient was **added within a look-back window** [P] needs fresh step-up confirmation at execution. Additions of recipients across many funds in a short window raise a cross-fund flag. This answers the red-team counterexample B1 ([reviews](../13-adversarial-reviews/role-reviews.md)). |

heading: 2. Grant (sponsor side)
text:
| GR-1 | The grant's amount is a **fixed currency amount at reservation**, with three exceptions:
- *residual sweep* (FI-15): fixed after the last settlement;
- *proceeds-linked* grants, such as "the proceeds of my stock gift": fixed at the contribution's sale settlement;
- split disbursement where policy allows partial payment (FI-13).
A percentage recommendation is fixed exactly once (FI-10). A NAV later restated does **not** re-fix an approved grant; the correction is borne by the fund (FI-28). Round 2 G-29 asks the owner to confirm this (OD-07). |

heading: 2. Grant (sponsor side)
text: | GR-2 | No attempt may be created while any hold is active (SM-4). |

heading: 2. Grant (sponsor side)
text: | GR-3 | Cancelling a grant **abandons its pre-submission attempts (Prepared/Authorized) in the same operation**. Cancellation is impossible while an attempt is in Submitted, Unknown, Accepted or StopRequested; there it becomes a recall or stop request (GR-9). |

heading: 2. Grant (sponsor side)
text: | GR-4 | A reservation is released only on Canceled or Declined, or is consumed at settlement. Any **difference** between the reserved and the consumed amount is released at consumption with a recorded reason (FX buffer, liquidation buffer, provider fee policy). Without that rule such residue becomes Stranded by design (financial review A-8; round 2 G-10). |

heading: 2. Grant (sponsor side)
text: | GR-5 | Donor copy: "Payment sent on D" when cumulative settlement is observed. "Paid" may be used only once `Final(rail)` holds, or with a qualifier ([status vocabulary](../09-ux/status-vocabulary.md)). This resolves the round 2 G-24 conflict. |

heading: 2. Grant (sponsor side)
text: | GR-6 | A flag raised after any attempt is Submitted opens a **post-payment review** child case. It does not change grant state. Recovery from the recipient is a separate case with human authority. |

heading: 2. Grant (sponsor side)
text: | GR-7 | Fund `Suspended`, `Frozen` or authority `Disputed` holds every grant without a live attempt. That **includes re-payment after a return** (round 2 G-14). Attempts already submitted resolve normally. |

heading: 2. Grant (sponsor side)
text: | GR-8 | After sponsor approval, the requester's later loss of authority (death, revocation) does **not** cancel the grant. The sponsor approved it under its own authority, and completing it is the default [P][C] (OD-03). Standing recommendations are suspended until authority is re-established. |

heading: 2. Grant (sponsor side)
text: | GR-9 | A cancellation request has its own lifecycle: Requested → Granted (grant Canceled) / Refused (with reason) / Overtaken (settlement arrived first). Each outcome has a label (round 2 G-22). |

heading: 2. Grant (sponsor side)
text: | GR-10 | **One ordering key.** Capacity contention is decided by the reservation sequence number alone. "Approval order", "FIFO" and client-supplied `effective_at` are not ordering keys. This resolves the financial review A-4 and round 2 G-17. Routine approval and reservation are one atomic step. Human-approved grants that fail capacity wait in `ApprovedAwaitingCapacity`, with an expiry and the label "Approved – waiting for funds" (OD-06). |

heading: 2. Grant (sponsor side)
text: | GR-11 | Returned money re-reserved for re-payment **restores a prior commitment**. It is exempt from FI-12's refusal of new reservations, but not from fund holds (GR-7) or closure (FUND-1). This resolves the round 2 G-15 conflict. |

heading: 2. Grant (sponsor side)
text: | GR-12 | Who funds a replacement grant after a misdirected or forged payment is a sponsor error-cost decision (OD-20). It is never silently charged to the donor's fund (round 2 G-27; cross X-15). |

heading: 3. Payment attempt
text: | PA-1 | **Cumulative double-payment invariant.** For each grant: Σ amounts of attempts in {Authorized, Submitted, Unknown, Accepted, StopRequested, Settled-not-returned} ≤ grant amount. Exceptions are allowed only through PA-2 decisions and `Lost` claims, which carry an explicit duplicate-risk acceptance. This permits split disbursement and per-payment rail caps (round 2 G-3). |

heading: 3. Payment attempt
text: | PA-2 | `Unknown → NotReceived` requires **two sources**: provider proof of non-receipt, and the bank statement showing no debit by the provider's settlement horizon (cross X-17; ontology §3). If neither is obtainable, only `ResolvedByDecision` remains: two approvers, the releaser excluded, a recorded duplicate-risk acceptance and a recovery plan. |

heading: 3. Payment attempt
text: | PA-3 | A retry of the *same* attempt reuses its key, but only **within the provider's contracted deduplication window**. After the window, a retry is a new attempt and must pass PA-2 first (round 2 G-6). |

heading: 3. Payment attempt
text: | PA-4 | Checks: issued and unpresented = `Accepted`. The reservation is **consumed at issue into an outstanding-check liability**, so capacity is not reduced twice by FI-21 and GR-4 (financial review A-2). Void is `Accepted → StopRequested → Voided`, and only after the **bank confirms** the stop (positive pay). Reissue is possible only after `Voided`. Dormant checks follow the unclaimed-property process [C: REG-045 is unverified]. |

heading: 3. Payment attempt
text: | PA-5 | `Unknown` and `Accepted` have aging deadlines [P]. When a deadline passes, the attempt goes to the exception queue with a named owner. No attempt waits indefinitely (red team B9; round 2 G-2). |

heading: 3. Payment attempt
text: | PA-6 | **Contradicting evidence.** If a terminal attempt (Failed, NotReceived, Returned, Voided, ResolvedByDecision) later meets evidence of settlement, or a return arrives before its settlement notice, a **double-payment case** opens and further attempts on the grant are blocked until it is resolved. A table of which observations imply which must be part of each provider adapter's contract (round 2 G-5). |

heading: 3. Payment attempt
text: | PA-7 | Batch files: a file-level submission has its own idempotency key and its own Unknown. Partial acceptance is recorded per item. A file Unknown makes every item Unknown (round 2 G-7). |

heading: 3. Payment attempt
text: | PA-8 | **Funds in transit.** Once the sponsor's bank is debited and before the recipient is credited (an intermediary or a pre-funded provider), the amount is a **receivable from the provider**, not fund cash. `Lost` converts it to a claim. Which party bears the loss is OD-20 (round 2 G-8; cross X-18). |

heading: 3. Payment attempt
text: | PA-9 | Late return edge: returns of **outbound credits** after the normal return window are rail-specific and limited [I]. The earlier draft's "unauthorized-debit class" example applies to debits, i.e. contributions, not to grant payments (red team B3; financial review A-6). |

heading: 5. Contribution
text: - CON-1: `Provisional` value cannot fund a `Reserved` grant beyond a sponsor-set **provisional credit limit** per donor or fund. The default proposed is zero [P] (OD-04).

heading: 5. Contribution
text: - CON-2: An acknowledgment for a reversible contribution is issued only after `Final`, or carries a correction path that is tested [C].

heading: 5. Contribution
text: - CON-3: A `Reversed` contribution whose value already funded a disbursed grant creates a **sponsor receivable from the donor** and a fund deficit case. It never creates a negative fund silently.

heading: 6. Fund (account)
text: - FUND-3: merge, split and transfer produce a **lineage routing table**. Late events, templates, flags, holds and successor plans are routed or explicitly ended (TVF-128).

heading: 6. Fund (account)
text: - FUND-4: sponsor succession (merger, dissolution, revocation of the sponsoring organization) is a separate workflow (W-NEW, TVF-130) [C].

heading: 6. Fund (account)
text: - FUND-2: A fund cannot leave `Frozen` through any automated path.

heading: 7. Authority grant and succession
text: | AUTH-I1 | An authority change takes effect at command execution. Sessions, widget instances, cached projections, partner tokens and delegated agent privileges derived from the old authority are invalidated, or re-checked on next use. The maximum staleness window is a stated requirement, not an emergent property ([TVF-015](../16-registers/findings.csv)). |

heading: 7. Authority grant and succession
text: | AUTH-I2 | Delegated grants (advisor, agent, partner user) derive from a parent authority. When the parent ends, the children end at the same effective time. |

heading: 7. Authority grant and succession
text: | AUTH-I3 | When the triggering fact is effective in the past (date of death reported two weeks later), actions taken in between under the dead principal's authority are **flagged for review**, not reversed automatically. Approved grants are governed by GR-8 [C]. |

heading: 7. Authority grant and succession
text: | AUTH-I4 | Two successors with joint authority: the policy must define quorum. Without it, recommendations require all. |

heading: 7. Authority grant and succession
text: | AUTH-I5 | **Death or incapacity notice from an unauthenticated channel** is a flag, not a fact (red team B7). The immediate effect is limited to holding *new* recommendations and template instances from the named person. The person is notified through their verified channel. Approved grants continue (GR-8). A false notice therefore delays at most the person's own new requests, and the false notice is itself recorded. |

heading: 7. Authority grant and succession
text: | AUTH-I6 | **Third-party authority registers** (custodian trading authorizations, bank-portal approvers, provider user lists) are in scope for AUTH-I1, with a revocation SLA and evidence (TVF-123). |

heading: 7. Authority grant and succession
text: | AUTH-I7 | **Authority-relevant credential changes** need step-up and a cooling-off period, plus notice to the prior channel. Examples: enrolling a new authenticator or passkey, changing email or phone, changing a recovery factor. Grants to recipients added during that cooling-off period need sponsor-direct confirmation (red team B1; round 2 S-7). |

heading: 7. Authority grant and succession
text: | AUTH-I8 | Partner identity mapping uses a permanent identifier (issuer plus subject, or the SCIM external ID), never an email or reusable login ID. A mapping change needs dual control and notice to the donor (TVF-138). |

heading: 10. Time basis (round 2 G-19, G-20; S-20)
text: | TIME-1 | Every deadline (cooling-off, freshness SLO, return window, aging, due date) names its calendar: business days per the rail's calendar, or calendar days. It also names its time zone: the sponsor's legal-entity zone for donor-facing dates, UTC for system ordering. |

heading: 10. Time basis (round 2 G-19, G-20; S-20)
text: | TIME-2 | Effective time and recorded time are both kept (SM-1). Ordering and freshness use **recorded time from an authoritative time source**. Detected clock skew beyond tolerance fails closed for money movement. |

heading: 10. Time basis (round 2 G-19, G-20; S-20)
text: | TIME-3 | Year-end attribution: the period and tax-year attribution of a late-observed settlement, a cross-year return or void, and an Unknown at year-end are set by a reporting recognition policy [C] (OD-19). |

heading: 2.1 Conservation and ledger
text: | FI-01 | Every journal balances in each currency. No posting into a closed period through any write path. Corrections are reversals or adjustments. | Every posting | Reject (baseline invariant 3) |

heading: 2.1 Conservation and ledger
text: | FI-02 | Σ account units × NAV = pool NAV within tolerance; Σ pool positions = custodian positions after known in-transit items. | Each NAV strike; daily | Block NAV publication (WF-18; CTL-017) |

heading: 2.1 Conservation and ledger
text: | FI-03 | Legal-owner cash (sponsor entity) per custodial and bank account = Σ fund cash claims + sponsor operating cash + suspense + **in-transit** (debited, not yet observed) − **outstanding checks** + **provider receivables** (PA-8). | Daily | Break case. Rev 2: reservations are blocked only up to the **unexplained break amount** above a materiality threshold [P], not on the whole shared account. Otherwise one timing break halts every donor (review A-11). |

heading: 2.1 Conservation and ledger
text: | FI-04 | Suspense and unapplied cash have an owner and an age. Nothing ages out of suspense into a fund or into revenue without a human decision. | Daily | Escalate by age |

heading: 2.2 Capacity and reservation
text: | FI-05 | A reservation of amount *a* is created only if *a* ≤ `C(x,t)` for the fund **and every constrained ancestor x** (pool cash buffer if paying ahead of liquidation, custodial account, legal entity, restricted sub-balance). Check and creation are one serialized operation per ancestor, with locks taken in a fixed order. | Reservation | Reject; grant stays `Approved` and held "insufficient capacity" (or approval and reservation are atomic, so approval fails) |

heading: 2.2 Capacity and reservation
text: | FI-06 | Displayed "available to recommend" = `C(f,t)` minus soft pending claims, labelled as an estimate with its as-of time. It is never shown as cash. | Each render | Content rule |

heading: 2.2 Capacity and reservation
text: | FI-07 | A reservation is released only by cancellation, decline or consumption at settlement. Never by timeout, Unknown, a projection rebuild, or a UI action. | Each release | Reject release |

heading: 2.2 Capacity and reservation
text: | FI-08 | Two recommendations, from one or many advisors, cannot both be approved if together they exceed `C` at the moment of the later reservation. Approval order is the serialization order of reservations, not the submission order. | Reservation | The later one fails capacity; the requester is told it was approved-pending-capacity or declined, per OD-06 |

heading: 2.2 Capacity and reservation
text: | FI-09 | Recurring grants reserve **per instance**, at the instance's due date, never for the series. | Each instance | Instance held |

heading: 2.3 Fixed and percentage grants across several investments
text: | FI-10 | **Single fixing.** A percentage grant is converted to a currency amount exactly once, at a defined fixing event, with a recorded valuation snapshot ID. Proposed default: fix at approval, using the latest struck NAV [P; OD-07]. The donor-visible preview is an *estimate at preview time*. After fixing, the grant is an ordinary fixed-amount grant. |

heading: 2.3 Fixed and percentage grants across several investments
text: | FI-11 | **Allocation is a funding plan, not a set of grants.** Lines `{source_i, share_i}` say where the cash comes from. The sponsor controls investments (DD-007), so a donor allocation is itself a recommendation. Line amounts = fixed amount × share, rounded to minor units by largest remainder with deterministic tie-break on source ID. Σ line amounts = grant amount exactly. |

heading: 2.3 Fixed and percentage grants across several investments
text: | FI-12 | **Over-commitment.** If market moves make `R(f,t) > V(f,t) − H`, the fund is over-committed. New reservations are refused, except re-reservations after a return (GR-11). Already-approved grants keep their fixed amounts. Unfunded grants are funded in **reservation sequence order** (GR-10). Any remaining shortfall is a sponsor decision case (cancel newest, top-up policy, or partial) [P; OD-08]. The fund never goes negative silently. |

heading: 2.3 Fixed and percentage grants across several investments
text: | FI-13 | **Source shortfall.** If one source cannot deliver its line (illiquid, restricted, gated, custodian outage), the grant enters `FundingShortfall`. Policy decides: re-plan to other permitted sources (allowed when the donor's allocation was a preference) or hold. No partial payment unless sponsor policy explicitly allows split disbursement [P]. |

heading: 2.3 Fixed and percentage grants across several investments
text: | FI-14 | **Funding in unitized pools (rev 2; review A-3).** Units redeemed per source = line amount ÷ forward NAV at strike. That redemption is internal and exact in currency. The pool meets cash needs by **net** trading across all flows (contributions, grants, fees, rebalancing) under treasury policy. Per-grant trades exist only for non-pooled (separately managed) sources. The grant receives exactly its fixed amount unless sponsor policy allows partial payment (FI-13). Pool liquidity shortfall is a pool-level event (WF-17), not a grant-level one. |

heading: 2.3 Fixed and percentage grants across several investments
text: | FI-15 | **"100% of fund" or closing grant** is a distinct type: a *residual sweep*. Its amount is not known until all fees through closing date, all other obligations and all liquidations have settled. It is fixed after the last settlement, not at approval. A 100% grant fixed at approval is guaranteed to be wrong in one direction or the other. |

heading: 2.3 Fixed and percentage grants across several investments
text: | FI-16 | **Percentage of what.** Allowed denominators are an enumerated set, each with a definition: fund `V`, reservable capacity `C`, a named portfolio's value, or a sponsor spendable base (endowed funds). "Percent of account" without a type is invalid. |

heading: 2.4 Settlement, payment and return
text: | FI-17 | Settlement conservation (baseline): on confirmed settlement of *X*, in one transaction, record unique external evidence, reduce confirmed cash by *X*, reduce the matching reservation by *X*, post the journal, write the outbox. Failure leaves the prior state plus an exception. |

heading: 2.4 Settlement, payment and return
text: | FI-18 | Double-payment invariant PA-1 ([state models §3](../06-state-models/state-models.md#3-payment-attempt)). |

heading: 2.4 Settlement, payment and return
text: | FI-19 | A return after settlement **re-credits the fund in cash** (the units were already redeemed). Reinvestment of returned cash follows the fund's allocation policy at the next cycle. The grant goes to `Returned` and its new reservation is re-established from that cash, not from new units. |

heading: 2.4 Settlement, payment and return
text: | FI-20 | A recipient refund (charity sends money back, for example a canceled event or excess benefit discovered) is **not** a return. It is a new inbound receipt linked to the grant. Whether it goes back to the fund or elsewhere, and whether it reverses the grant for Schedule D, are [C] questions (OD-09). |

heading: 2.4 Settlement, payment and return
text: | FI-21 | Uncashed checks: at issue, the reservation is **consumed into an outstanding-check liability**, counted once (PA-4). Void (bank-confirmed) → re-credit or reissue per policy. Dormancy → unclaimed-property process [C: REG-045 is UNVERIFIED]. |

heading: 2.5 Contributions
text: | FI-22 | Contribution value on a reversible rail is `Provisional` until the reversal window passes. Provisional value counts toward `V` for display and fees but is excluded from `C` except up to the provisional credit limit (CON-1). |

heading: 2.5 Contributions
text: | FI-23 | A reversed contribution produces a reversal entry dated when the reversal is recorded, with effective date = original. Units issued against it are cancelled at the current NAV. **Rev 2 (review A-5):** the difference between the NAV at issue and at cancellation would otherwise fall on other unitholders. The policy must say which net assets absorb it, and an uncollectible receivable [C]. If the units no longer exist, the shortfall is a donor receivable and sponsor exposure, never a silent negative balance (CON-3). Fees and partner revenue share accrued on reversed value are reversed (round 2 X-10). |

heading: 2.5 Contributions
text: | FI-24 | Non-cash gift value: acceptance value, custody receipt value, gift-date valuation for acknowledgment, and sale proceeds are four different numbers. Only sale proceeds fund grants. |

heading: 2.6 Fees
text: | FI-25 | Fee accrual reduces `V` and `C` when accrued, not when collected. Otherwise a fund can reserve its whole balance and leave nothing for the fee. |

heading: 2.6 Fees
text: | FI-26 | If accrued fees exceed `V − R` (an over-committed fund), the order of priority between the fee and approved grants is a sponsor policy decision [P; OD-10]. It must be decided before it occurs, not during an incident. |

heading: 2.6 Fees
text: | FI-27 | Fees computed on a stale or later-restated NAV are recalculated by an adjustment entry in the current period, with an effective date. The fee basis records the NAV version used (FEE-03, FEE-11). |

heading: 2.7 Corrections and external disagreement
text: | FI-28 | **Custodian historical correction.** A correction to positions or cash effective in a past period is recorded bitemporally. If it changes a struck NAV beyond the materiality tolerance, a NAV-error case decides between restatement (re-processing unit transactions at the corrected NAV) and current-period adjustment [P/C; industry practice for pooled vehicles is a materiality threshold, I]. Fund-level effects on already-redeemed units are computed and shown, not ignored. |

heading: 2.7 Corrections and external disagreement
text: | FI-29 | When the ledger, custodian and bank disagree, no source wins by default. Each field has a declared authoritative source (DATA-07). A disagreement creates a break that blocks new reservations on the affected resource when its amount exceeds a threshold [P]. |

heading: 2.7 Corrections and external disagreement
text: | FI-30 | An external balance feed is an observation. It never makes cash spendable on its own (baseline). |

heading: 2.7a Charges, fees and residues (rev 2)
text: | FI-36 | Every income and cost item has an owner and a destination: interest on in-transit cash, rounding residue, wire and return fees, credit-line interest, bank charges on incoming foreign wires. Defaults [P]: platform-caused costs are sponsor costs; rail charges follow the grant's recorded **charge bearer**, so a deducted foreign-bank fee never silently breaks the GR-1 fixed amount (review A-9; round 2 X-8). |

heading: 2.7a Charges, fees and residues (rev 2)
text: | FI-37 | **Fund charges and commitments** that are neither grants nor fees are a distinct fact, and known commitments reduce `C(f,t)`. Examples: capital calls on held private assets, carrying costs, UBIT/990-T [C] (round 2 X-8). |

heading: 2.7a Charges, fees and residues (rev 2)
text: | FI-38 | **Inter-fund correction.** Sponsor or third-party errors (misapplied receipt, mis-sourced grant, duplicate trade) are corrected by an inter-fund reclassification record. The party at fault makes the fund whole under an error-cost policy (OD-20; round 2 X-15). |

text: ### TVCTL-05 Protective-check completion before release (resolves TVC-007) | Field | Value | |---|---| | Objective | No routine grant is released while a protective screen has not completed, or its deterministic fallback has not run | | Risk | §4967 benefit; reputational | | Authority | CRCO | | Trigger | Every routine grant | | Evidence | Decision record shows agent result or fallback result | | Failure response | Hold | | Monitoring | Fallback rate; agent latency | | Independent verification | QA sample of fallback-path grants | | Exceptions | None | | Mapping | TSC processing integrity |

heading: TVCTL-05 Protective-check completion before release (resolves TVC-007)
text: ### TVCTL-06 Assurance-bound auto-approval (resolves TVC-025/026) | Field | Value | |---|---| | Objective | No grant is auto-approved beyond the assurance of the session or principal that requested it; new recipients from phishable or agent sessions need step-up confirmation | | Risk | Account takeover (FM-12); prompt-injected agents | | Authority | CRCO + security | | Trigger | Every recommendation | | Evidence | Session assurance, `amr`, confirmation event | | Failure response | Route to confirmation or hold | | Monitoring | Holds for unconfirmed new recipients; confirmed-to-requested ratio | | Independent verification | Red-team exercise annually [P] | | Exceptions | None | | Mapping | TSC CC6 (logical access) |

heading: TVCTL-07 Reconciliation independence (resolves TVC-028)
text: ### TVCTL-08 NAV-error and restatement control Objective: errors in struck NAV from custodian corrections are evaluated against materiality and corrected consistently (FI-28). Authority: Controller (R); CFO plus an independent reviewer (A). Evidence: NAV-error case with computation. Failure response: affected statements corrected. Independent verification: auditor. Mapping: ICFR.

heading: TVCTL-08 NAV-error and restatement control
text: ### TVCTL-09 Policy delegation linkage (resolves TVC-003 in part) Objective: every D approval cites a policy version that is linked to an effective board delegation. Evidence: per-decision link. Failure response: if a delegation lapses, dependent policies suspend (routine path → human). Independent verification: Audit Committee annual review. Mapping: governance; REG-001 [C].

heading: TVCTL-09 Policy delegation linkage (resolves TVC-003 in part)
text: ### TVCTL-10 Authority-change propagation Objective: authority changes reach every derived session, token, widget instance and recurring template within the stated window (AUTH-I1, TVR-WID-001/006). Evidence: propagation log with timestamps. Failure response: incident. Monitoring: p99 propagation time. Independent verification: quarterly test revocations. Mapping: TSC CC6.

heading: TVCTL-10 Authority-change propagation
text: ### TVCTL-11 Control-evidence integrity (resolves TVF-041) Objective: control evidence cannot be altered by the function whose controls it evidences. Authority: internal audit (A). Evidence: append-only store with hash chain; access logs. Failure response: evidence gap logged as control failure. Independent verification: auditor. Mapping: TSC CC4/CC7.

heading: TVCTL-11 Control-evidence integrity (resolves TVF-041)
text: ### TVCTL-13 OFAC blocking and reject reporting (rev 2; review A5) Objective: when a payment or asset involves a blocked person, funds are **blocked** (not merely recalled to the fund) or rejected as required. Reports are filed within the regulatory deadline. Records are kept for at least 10 years (REG-037 [F]; application to DAFs [C]). Implementation and ownership: - Authority: sanctions officer (R), GC (A). - Requires a `Blocked` disposition in the payment attempt and contribution models, with a blocked-property account. - Failure response: escalate to the GC immediately. - Independent verification: internal audit annually. Note: TVCTL-04 is a pre-payment gate and **does not** cover REG-037 reporting (review correction).

heading: TVCTL-13 OFAC blocking and reject reporting (rev 2; review A5)
text: ### TVCTL-14 Disqualified-recipient and excess-benefit gate (rev 2; reviews A8, A18) Objective: the routine path excludes recipients and payees where: - §4966 requires expenditure responsibility, or where the grant is a taxable distribution, e.g. Type III non-functionally-integrated supporting organizations and donor-controlled supporting organizations [unverified detail, C]; - §4958(c)(2) treats any payment to a donor, advisor or related person as automatic excess benefit (REG-004 [F]). Implementation: deterministic classification from IRS codes and the relationship graph. A match routes to a human, never to auto-approve. Independent verification: QA sample.

heading: TVCTL-14 Disqualified-recipient and excess-benefit gate (rev 2; reviews A8, A18)
text: ### TVCTL-12 Expenditure responsibility obligation tracker (fills REG-002 gap) Objective: every ER grant has pre-grant inquiry, agreement terms, reports and Schedule D/990 reporting inputs tracked to completion. Authority: grants compliance head. Evidence: per-grant obligation record. Failure response: missing report → escalation and hold on further grants to that grantee. Independent verification: annual sample. Mapping: REG-002 [K → C].
